articles.title: Apuestas y pronósticos Getafe vs Celta
articles.standfirst: Retabet te ofrece el pronóstico del partido que enfrenta al Getafe y al Celta en el Coliseum correspondiente a la cuarta jornada de LaLiga
articles.summary: Retabet te ofrece el pronóstico del partido que enfrenta al Getafe y al Celta en el Coliseum correspondiente a la cuarta jornada de LaLiga
articles.body: El Getafe recibe al Celta este lunes en el Coliseum, en el partido correspondiente a la cuarta jornada de LaLiga 26/27. El conjunto azulón afronta el encuentro con la necesidad de reencontrarse con la victoria tras caer por 1-0 ante Osasuna en El Sadar, un resultado que deja al equipo de José Bordalás con solo tres puntos de nueve posibles y con un dato preocupante. Apenas ha marcado un gol en las tres jornadas disputadas hasta el momento. Favorito para el partido entre Getafe y Celta Por su parte, el Celta llega a tierras madrileñas todavía en busca de su primera victoria de la temporada. El conjunto de Claudio Giráldez disputó entre semana su partido aplazado de la sexta jornada ante la Real Sociedad en Anoeta, que finalizó con empate a cero, después de haber caído previamente por 0-2 ante el Athletic Club en Balaídos. Los gallegos tampoco han sido nada prolíficos de cara a puerta, con un único gol anotado en los cuatro partidos que llevan disputados esta campaña. Con todos estos datos, las casas de apuestas dan como favorito al Getafe, aunque sin una diferencia demasiado amplia, dado el nivel similar de necesidad que atraviesan ambos conjuntos. Retabet paga la victoria local a cuota 2.44, por 2.89 del empate y 3.40 de la victoria del cuadro celeste. Ambos equipos marcan El mercado de ambos equipos marcan aparece como una de las alternativas más arriesgadas del encuentro. El Getafe solo ha marcado un gol en sus tres primeras jornadas, y el Celta tampoco ha sido capaz de superar esa cifra en sus cuatro partidos disputados, con dos de ellos terminando sin goles por parte de ninguno de los dos conjuntos. Con estos datos, según las apuestas deportivas, la balanza se inclina claramente hacia el "no". Retabet paga a 2.37 el "sí" y a 1.58 el "no". Número total de goles (Over/Under) El mercado de goles apunta hacia un partido de corte muy contenido. Tanto el Getafe como el Celta arrastran serios problemas para generar peligro de cara a puerta, y sus últimos precedentes, con un 0-0 y una derrota mínima respectivamente, invitan a pensar en un encuentro cerrado y con pocas ocasiones claras. Retabet sitúa la cuota del +2.5 totales a 2.82, por 1.39 del caso contrario. Número total de córners (Over/Under) El mercado de córners se presenta como una alternativa interesante para los apostantes. El Getafe, con un planteamiento defensivo y de bloque bajo característico de José Bordalás, no suele generar un volumen elevado de saques de esquina, aunque sí puede beneficiarse de las pérdidas del rival en campo propio. El Celta, por su parte, ha mostrado en sus últimos partidos un juego con poca profundidad y escasas llegadas por banda, lo que también invita a pensar en un número de córners más bien ajustado en los dos sentidos a lo largo del encuentro.

articles.title: 'Multiple Firings' Likely After Michigan vs. Western Michigan Finish
articles.summary: Firings are coming soon, it appears.
articles.body:
The Big Ten Conference is standing by the controversial Michigan vs. Western Michigan finish on Saturday night, but that doesn't mean everyone is going to keep their jobs.

Michigan topped Western Michigan, 13-12, as time expired at Michigan Stadium. The Wolverines were gifted 0:01 after the clock appeared to hit 0:00. Michigan used that remaining second to take down Western Michigan with an impossible Hail Mary! play.

While fans are calling for an investigation, the Big Ten Conference is standing by the ruling.

"Following video review, it was determined Western Michigan's #18 started his jump from an established out-of-bounds position (left foot) and made contact with the ball with one second remaining on the clock. As shown in the provided video of what was viewed during the replay process, a side-by-side view of the play and the game clock, using a direct shot of the game clock in the stadium, was used to determine the final ruling. Eighty-five minutes prior to the game, all broadcast cameras used for the replay system, including the camera on the game clock, are synced using a strobe system to ensure all cameras are aligned," the Big Ten Conference said.

"Per NCAA Football rule 4-2-3-a, "A ball not in player control, other than a kick that scores a field goal, is out of bounds when it touches the ground, a player, a game official or anything else that is out-of-bound, or that is on or outside a boundary line," and thus the clock is stopped."

College sports insider Dan Wolken believes firings are coming, though.

The Yahoo! Sports columnist is predicting that multiple people will be losing their jobs – and quickly.

"This is truly the worst thing that could happen for the Big Ten. This is a major college football scandal that is going to resonate beyond sports coverage and, I predict, cost someone or multiple people their jobs. It cannot happen. I want investigations and firings now," he shared.

We now wait to see if anything will happen firing-wise following the controversial Week 1 finish.

articles.title: ‘A long-time dream’: Nihal Sarin 'excited' but 'not thinking about' India's Chess Olympiad title defence
articles.summary: Chess News: BENGALURU: The Chess Olympiad is already on Indian Grandmaster Nihal Sarin’s mind, but not quite yet. With India preparing to defend its Open title in.
articles.body: BENGALURU: The Chess Olympiad is already on Indian Grandmaster Nihal Sarin’s mind, but not quite yet. With India preparing to defend its Open title in Samarkand, Uzbekistan later this month, Nihal is excited about representing the country at the Olympiad. For now, though, the 22-year-old is keeping his attention firmly on the Global Chess League (GCL), where he is representing American Gambits in this fourth season.Asked whether he was already thinking about the Olympiad while playing his games in Bengaluru, Nihal said: “Not really, no. Like, in general, I'm just extremely excited to play in the Olympiad. I'm very happy, and I'll just try to give my best for the team. It has been a long-time dream.”But with the GCL currently taking centre stage, Nihal is deliberately keeping things relaxed. “Now I'm just (focusing on GCL). This tournament is very relaxed. I'm just trying to chill on and off the board,” he said after American Gambits’ match against Ganges Grandmasters on Sunday.India’s title defence will carry considerable expectations. Four members of the Budapest-winning squad return, although there will understandably be significant changes to the board order. Arjun Erigaisi leads the five-player lineup on 2759, followed by Praggnanandhaa R on 2750. Nihal, rated 2718, will replace Pentala Harikrishna.World Champion Gukesh Dommaraju is also there, while Vidit Gujrathi completes the squad. Srinath Narayanan returns as captain.At the 2024 Olympiad in Budapest, Gukesh played on board one and delivered a phenomenal 9/10 score with a 3056 performance rating, winning individual gold as India finished four match points clear. Arjun also claimed individual gold on board three.Nevertheless, defending the title will be no easy task. Armenia remains the last team to successfully retain the Open crown, winning in 2006 and 2008. The last five editions have produced four different champions, underlining how difficult sustained dominance has been.What happened in GCL on Day 2 Defending champions APL Pipers made it two wins from two, beating Ganges Grandmasters 11-6, while Ganges bounced back later to defeat American Gambits 9-7. Nihal won his game against Levon Aronian with black pieces in a nerve-wracking battle, but it was not enough for his team. Alaskan Knights beat Mumba Masters 11-6, before Mumba Masters edged Triveni Continental Kings 10-9 in the final match of the day.At this moment, American Gambits lead the standings on 6 match points and 31 game points, ahead of Ganges Grandmasters on 6/25. Alpine APL Pipers are third with 6/21, while Mumba Masters and Alaskan Knights have 3 match points each. articles.title: TOI Exclusive: Personal coaches push gains momentum in equestrian, selectors’ dual roles raise questions
articles.summary: More sports News: NEW DELHI: With the Asian Games barely weeks away, a curious battle over coaches is brewing in Indian equestrian — five riders have sought accreditati.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: With the Asian Games barely weeks away, a curious battle over coaches is brewing in Indian equestrian — five riders have sought accreditation for their foreign personal coaches, even as officials involved in selecting the team are themselves headed to Japan in coaching and team-management roles.The demand has put the spotlight on how the equestrian contingent’s coaching support was finalised, particularly because the foreign coaches being sought by the riders have trained them through the international season and are now being preferred over some of the Indian coaches cleared by the sports authorities.TOI has learnt that at least five of the seven dressage and eventing riders have sought to take their personal coaches to the Games. The five are Shruti Vora (athlete) — Rebecca Moody (British, coach); Ashish Limaye — Carola Bierlein (German); Gaurav Pundir — Brian Barnett (Dutch); Arjan Nagra — Felix Etzel (German); and Jai Sud — Antonie de Ridder (Dutch).All five have approached the Indian Olympic Association (IOA)-run ad-hoc committee for governance of the Equestrian Federation of India (EFI), seeking accreditation for their personal coaches.The issue gets more intriguing when viewed alongside the composition of the selection committees. Documents accessed by TOI show Col Sandeep Dewan, Jai Rathore (who also goes by the name Mrityunjay Sinh Rathore and Jay Rathore) and Kapil Modi were on the dressage selection committee, while Col Amit Sinsinwar and Imitiaz Anees were on the three-day eventing selection committee. Dewan and Imitiaz were also part of the technical committee.Several of these officials are now travelling with the contingent. The sanctioned coaching/support staff included Anees, Rathore and Sinsinwar as coaches, with Dewan as team leader.Sources said the overlap between those involved in selecting the Asian Games team and those accompanying it has raised questions about a potential conflict of interest, though there is no suggestion of wrongdoing against any individual.The issue is particularly pointed in Shruti’s case. Sources said the dressage rider has written to the authorities stating that Rathore has not coached her and that she has been trained by Moody. She has sought Moody’s accreditation instead.There is also the Sinsinwar episode. India’s show jumping squad was dropped after failing to meet the selection criteria, leaving the country to compete only in dressage and three-day eventing. Yet Sinsinwar, nominated as show jumping coach, was initially included in the sanctioned contingent.The anomaly was subsequently corrected. In a mail accessed by TOI, the IOA told EFI’s ad-hoc committee that Sinsinwar was “not to be deputed to Japan” as the show jumping team had not been approved, and directed that his accreditation card be returned.The personal-coach issue, however, remains alive.In the same communication, the IOA said it was “taking the necessary steps” with the OCA and AINAGOC regarding the five personal coaches and getting them accreditation.Interestingly, EFI’s ad-hoc committee had separately recommended just two — Moody and Bierlein — saying they could also coach other members of the team.The questions now are hard to ignore: why were coaches sought by riders not part of the original support structure, why are officials involved in selection also travelling with the team, and was the initial coaching list the result of oversight — or simply the federation’s recommendation being accepted without enough scrutiny?Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Denver Summit down first-place Gotham at home 3-0
articles.summary: Yazmeen Ryan scored against her former team and Kat Asman made four crucial saves in the Denver Summit's 3-0 win on Sunday over visiting Gotham FC in the Nat...
articles.body:
Yazmeen Ryan scored against her former team and Kat Asman made four crucial saves in the Denver Summit's 3-0 win on Sunday over visiting Gotham FC in the National Women's Soccer League.

In the day's other matches, the North Carolina Courage stunned the Chicago Stars 6-0; the Washington Spirit came from behind to beat the Portland Thorns 2-1; the Orlando Pride overtook the Houston Dash 3-1; and the Seattle Reign beat the San Diego Wave 1-0.

Gotham (13-4-6) has sat atop the National Women's Soccer League standings for six weeks, with its last loss coming July 4 against the Wave. The expansion Summit had already beaten Gotham once this season, recording the first win in franchise history 2-0.

Denver (8-8-6) opened the scoring in the 50th minute when Yuzuki Yamamoto connected on the volley from Ayo Oke.

Rookie Olivia Thomas extended Denver's lead in the 82nd minute, driving into the box before ripping a shot past goalkeeper Ann-Katrin Berger.

Six minutes later, Ryan sent a shot to the bottom left corner out of Berger's reach.

Ashley Sanchez had a hat trick in North Carolina's 6-0 rout of the Stars (5-17-1) in Evanston, Illinois and now leads the league's Golden Boot race with 18 goals.

Sanchez, lurking at Chicago goalkeeper Kailen Sheridan's back post, capitalized on a cross and knocked a ball that was pinging around the box into the back of the net in the 11th minute.

Just six minutes later, Chioma Okafor pushed the lead to 2-0 with her first NWSL goal.

The Courage (12-8-3) combined for three goals in eight minutes in the second half. Shinomi Koyama scored in the 61st minute and two minutes later, Ryan Williams collected a rebound and put it away to make it 4-0.

Sanchez converted a penalty before capping her hat trick with a header off a cross from Williams. in the 81st minute

Bethi caps first Spirit start with winner

Mélissa Bethi scored her first league goal in her first start for the Spirit in the 80th minute in Portland.

Trinity Rodman beat the defenders down the sideline and crossed to Bethi for the goal.

The Thorns (11-7-5) set the tone early when Sophia Wilson converted a penalty in the 18th minute. Portland was awarded the kick after Monique Ngock pulled down Thorns midfielder Nina Nijstad in the box.

The Spirit (13-6-4) leveled the match in the 59th minute when Nijstad committed a foul against Bethi in the penalty box. After video review, Tara Rudd stepped up to score the lick.

Washington's Andi Sullivan was ejected in the seventh minute of stoppage time after a rough tackle just outside the penalty area.

Banda breaks Marta's single-season scoring record for the Pride

Barbra Banda made Orlando Pride history Sunday, converting a 42nd-minute penalty to become the club's single-season scoring leader.

Her 14th goal of the season surpassed Marta's record set in 2017, as the Pride went on to defeat the Houston Dash 3-1 in Orlando.

Banda's record-setting goal capped a first half in which Orlando took advantage of early Houston mistakes. Dash rookie Leah Klenke put the Pride ahead with an own goal in the 14th minute before conceding a penalty against Summer Yates 28 minutes later.

Banda sent her shot into the bottom left corner past goalkeeper Jane Campbell, giving Orlando a 2-0 lead heading into halftime.

Banda has scored in eight different home appearances this season, a feat achieved by only four players in NWSL history.

Orlando (9-12-2) stretched its advantage in the 64th minute on Haley McCutcheon's goal.

Houston (7-11-5) scored less than 10 minutes later when Khyah Harper's cross found Kiki Van Zanten, who headed the ball past goalkeeper Cosette Morché.

Maddie Mercado finished off a lofted cross from Maddie Dahlien with a header for a goal in the Reign's win at home.

Seattle (10-8-4) played with a player advantage over San Diego (12-8-3) for much of the match after Wave defender Amelia Van Zanten was shown a red card in the 13th minute. Van Zanten was sent off for a tackle from behind on Dahlien.

Reign goalkeeper Claudia Dickey made six saves before exiting the match following a collision with Wave forward Ludmila. Cassie Miller helped preserve Seattle's clean sheet.

articles.title: Who Won The NASCAR Cup Series Southern 500 at Darlington? Full Race Results
articles.summary: Christopher Bell opened The Chase for the NASCAR Cup Series by earning his first victory of the 2026 season. After passing Kyle Larson for the lead with 12 c...
articles.body:
Christopher Bell opened The Chase for the NASCAR Cup Series by earning his first victory of the 2026 season. After passing Kyle Larson for the lead with 12 circuits remaining, Bell captured the victory in Sunday night's Cook Out Southern 500 at the Darlington Raceway.

It was Bell's first Darlington win, first victory of the 2026 season and 14th career Cup win overall. The win was huge for Bell's championship hopes as he moved into the second position in the standings, 12 points behind leader Denny Hamlin.

It was a trying evening for Hamlin, who entered the Chase as the top seed. In the final stage, contact between Hamlin and Michael McDowell caused toe link damage on the No. 11 Joe Gibbs Racing Toyota.

The contact forced Hamlin to go a lap behind. The 45-year-old gained his lap back and ultimately finished 18th. Going into Darlington, Hamlin had a 25-point lead over second place Ryan Blaney. Now, the JGR driver has a 12-point edge over Bell.

William Byron had a difficult evening at Darlington as he posted a DNF of 37th place. The driver of the No. 24 suffered a flat tire in the final stage, then suffered an engine failure on the subsequent restart.

articles.title: Driver thanks rival for saving his life by stopping to pull him from flaming car
articles.summary: British driver Ollie Millroy thanked rival Loek Hartog for saving his life after the Dutch racer stopped and pulled him from a burning Ferrari during a China GT Championship race in Shanghai on Saturday.
articles.body: British driver Ollie Millroy thanked rival Loek Hartog for saving his life after the Dutch racer stopped and pulled him from a burning Ferrari during a China GT Championship race in Shanghai on Saturday. Millroy was involved in a multi-car crash on the seventh lap of the race and suffered five broken ribs, a broken collarbone, broken hand and finger, and a bruised lung. “I am still alive tonight, entirely thanks to one man,” Millroy posted on Instagram, describing how Hartog abandoned his own car and rushed to help before emergency crews arrived. “I don’t remember anything between 30 seconds before the crash and one hour after it, but I will remember his incredible act of bravery for the rest of my life,” Millroy said. Hartog said he had acted instinctively. “When I saw a car turning into a huge fireball far ahead, there wasn’t really a decision to make,” he said. “From what I had seen, I genuinely believed the driver might not be able to get out by himself. I stopped, got out and went towards the car. There was never a moment of doubt. It was scary.” Race organizers said they would investigate the incident and address shortcomings in competition management, emergency response, rescue operations and medical support. Millroy‘s team, AAI Motorsport, criticized the handling of the accident and said it would no longer compete in China GT events.

articles.title: ¿Por qué la boca de la gasolina está en unos coches a la derecha y en otros a la izquierda?: las razones que nadie cuenta
articles.standfirst: El pedal de freno, el intermitente o el propio volante siguen reglas casi universales, pero la tapa del depósito cambia de lado según el coche o la marca. Te contamos por qué no se ponen de acuerdo los fabricantes.
articles.summary: El pedal de freno, el intermitente o el propio volante siguen reglas casi universales, pero la tapa del depósito cambia de lado según el coche o la marca. Te contamos por qué no se ponen de acuerdo los fabricantes.
articles.body: Hoy casi todos los coches comparten el mismo lugar para el pedal de embrague (los que aún lo llevan) o para el acelerador. Los fabricantes llevan décadas 'puliendo' esas coincidencias para que cualquiera pueda sentarse en un coche desconocido y conducirlo casi sin pensar. Sin embargo, la boca de entrada del depósito sigue apareciendo en unos coches a la derecha y en otros a la izquierda. La explicación no tiene nada que ver con un capricho y obedece a razones de ingeniería, porque el lado elegido revela por dónde discurre el tubo de escape bajo los bajos del coche y cómo se ha repartido el resto de mecánica en esa zona. El motivo principal tiene que ver con el calor. El tubo de escape y el silenciador final son las piezas que más temperatura acumulan en los bajos de cualquier coche tras un rato circulando, y a los ingenieros les interesa mantener esa zona lejos del combustible en el momento de repostar. Por eso, la tapa de carga suele situarse en el lado contrario al del tramo final del escape, para evitar que un chorro, una salpicadura o un simple vapor de gasolina entre en contacto con el metal ardiendo. Averiguar dónde está el escape con solo mirar la tapa del depósito es, de hecho, muy sencillo. Pero esa no es la única razón, porque también se tiene en cuenta la seguridad del conductor y lo que puede pasar un día cualquiera en la carretera. Si nos quedáramos tirados y nos tocara repostar con una garrafa a pie de arcén, convendría estar en el lado alejado del tráfico. En España y en el resto de países que circulan por la derecha, ese lado seguro coincide con el lado del acompañante, así que buena parte de los fabricantes europeos y americanos colocan ahí la boca de carga. En Japón o el Reino Unido, donde se conduce por la izquierda, la lógica gira sobre sí misma y el lado protegido pasa a ser el otro. A esas dos razones se suma una tercera, esta obedeciendo al reglamento. La normativa exige que el depósito ocupe la parte más ancha de la carrocería, en una zona pensada para deformarse en un choque sin gotear sobre el tubo de escape ni sobre el cableado eléctrico. Esa exigencia explica por qué la tapa acaba siempre está en un lateral y descarta de un plumazo otras opciones, como la parte trasera (antes, muchos coches la llevaban aquí), donde un alcance por detrás resultaba mucho más peligroso. Con estas tres reglas sobre la mesa, cabría esperar un patrón claro según el país, pero la el proceso de fabricación añade una variable que lo revuelve todo aún más: las plataformas compartidas. Diseñar y fabricar una plataforma cuesta cientos de millones, así que las marcas usan la misma base para modelos que se venderán con el volante a la izquierda y a la derecha, y mover el depósito, las líneas de combustible y el tanque de un lado a otro según el mercado resultaría carísimo. El resultado es que la marca fija esa posición pensando en su mercado principal y la mantiene en todo el mundo, aunque eso obligue al comprador de otro país a rodear el coche entero para llegar hasta la tapa. Esta lógica explica, entre otras cosas, por qué marcas japonesas como Toyota o Subaru colocaron durante años la tapa en la aleta trasera izquierda, siguiendo la tradición del volante a la derecha de su mercado doméstico, aunque hoy conviven modelos que ya han cambiado de bando según la plataforma que utilicen. Para salir de dudas sin memorizar reglamentos ni geografía industrial, el cuadro de instrumentos guarda un chivatazo discreto: un pequeño triángulo o una flecha junto al icono del surtidor que apunta hacia el lado exacto donde está la tapa. Es uno de esos detalles que llevan ahí toda la vida y que casi nadie mira hasta que alguien se lo explica después de haberse quedado plantado, manguera en mano, en el lado equivocado del coche.

articles.title: Liam Farrell: Decorated Wigan Warriors captain to retire at end of season
articles.summary: Wigan Warriors captain Liam Farrell will retire at the end of the season after a 16-year career in which he has won 18 major honours.
articles.body:
Wigan Warriors captain Liam Farrell, one of the game's most decorated players, will end his playing career after this season.

The second row forward has won six Super Leagues, five League Leaders' Shields, five Challenge Cups and the World Club Challenge on two occasions.

Farrell, 36, has scored 151 tries in 428 games for his hometown club since his debut in 2010.

He was made captain before the 2023 season and was the skipper when Wigan won an unprecedented quadruple in 2024.

Capped 12 times by England, Farrell was contracted until the end of next season but has not played since the end of June because of a shoulder injury.

"It's been a whirlwind of a career, more than I could ever have dreamed of doing," he told the club's website. , external

"Although I'll be sad not to be playing any more, I'm also very grateful for the career I have had and I can now look forward to the next part of my life."

Wigan crush Leeds to move closer to winning shield

Farrell has a strong rugby league background, with his cousin being Wigan legend Andy, who is now head coach of Ireland's rugby union team.

Farrell came through the Warriors' academy system and made his debut as a teenager in April 2010.

By the end of that year, he had appeared in Wigan's Grand Final success over St Helens at Old Trafford, having also played a few games on loan at Widnes Vikings.

Since then, the forward has only ever played for the Cherry and Whites - a pillar of consistency in the pack.

As well as the team honours, Farrell has been included in the Super League Dream Team on six occasions, while he was also the Harry Sunderland Trophy winner as player of the match in the 2016 Grand Final win over Warrington Wolves.

He was the natural replacement to succeed Thomas Leulaui as Wigan skipper and his quiet authority has been at the forefront of a new glorious era under head coach Matt Peet.

Farrell has won seven of the 11 trophies available to Wigan during his time as captain, the most recent being the Challenge Cup at Wembley in May.

He could add two more before he retires, as Wigan chase the League Leaders' Shield this week and the Grand Final next month.

"You have to make the right call at the right time, and I think I have done that," he said. "Speaking to people close to me, professionals and the advice I have been given, it's the right time.

"Playing one game for Wigan was always the goal for me. If I had have done that and never played again I'd have been immensely proud, my family would have been proud and we'd have gone back to being Wigan fans.

"So to have been able to play over 400 games in this jersey has been nothing short of incredible."

Wigan chief executive Kris Radlinski has confirmed Farrell will remain at the club in a strength and conditioning role once he stops playing, and he paid tribute to one of the Warriors' finest ever who will make the move from the pitch into the backroom team.

"Liam will go down as one of Wigan's greatest players," Radlinski said.

"Sustaining excellence for so many years requires extraordinary commitment, resilience and mental strength.

"He has always put the team first, carried himself with quiet humility, and earned the respect of everyone connected with the club. His legacy is secure and he deserves to be celebrated."

articles.title: La historia que el pádel merecía: brutal, imperfecta y humana
articles.summary: La opinión de Jesús Mata
articles.body: Hay historias que uno recuerda por cómo empiezan, otras por todo lo que sucede en el camino y algunas, las verdaderamente importantes, por lo que transmiten. La de Gemma Triay y Ale Salazar pertenece a esta última categoría, porque después de todo lo que fueron juntas, de todo lo que ganaron y también de todo lo que ocurrió cuando aquella pareja que parecía indestructible dejó de existir, pocas imágenes podían poner un broche más bonito que la que nos regaló Madrid: las dos abrazadas, llorando, después de tantos años. Gemma y Ale fueron números uno, lo ganaron prácticamente todo y durante una época hicieron que ganar pareciera la consecuencia natural de jugar juntas. Fueron una pareja extraordinaria, de esas que terminan formando parte de la memoria de un deporte, pero también fueron humanas y su historia acabó mal, con dolor, desencuentros y dos versiones de lo ocurrido que ambas sintieron la necesidad de contar. MARCA estuvo ahí para escuchar a las dos, para dar voz a sus razones y a su manera de vivir aquella ruptura, y quizá por eso hoy tenga todavía más valor contemplar lo que sucedió en Madrid: no porque sepamos finalmente quién tenía razón, sino porque con los años hemos aprendido que hay batallas que no necesitan un ganador, sino un empate. Una semana antes del torneo, Ale Salazar reconocía en MARCA que le haría una ilusión tremenda retirarse ganando el Mundial junto a Gemma. La frase tenía algo un punto de imposible si uno recordaba cómo había terminado todo, pero también demostraba hasta qué punto el tiempo puede cambiar la perspectiva. Después llegó su adiós en el Movistar Arena de Madrid, instantes después de que Gemma alcanzase los 58 títulos, igualando precisamente la cifra que había convertido a su antigua compañera en una referencia histórica. Una preciosa casualidad. Y entonces llegó el abrazo, con las dos llorando, sin títulos de por medio, sin una pista que las separara y sin necesidad de explicar nada. Simplemente dos personas que habían compartido una parte enorme de sus vidas, que en algún momento se hicieron daño y que, muchos años después, fueron capaces de mirarse y abrazarse. Hay imágenes que emocionan porque cuentan una victoria; esta lo hace porque cuenta algo mucho más grande y, de alguna manera, te reconcilia con el pádel, con el deporte y hasta con la vida. Porque detrás de los números uno, los títulos y los rankings hay personas, y las personas nos equivocamos. Decimos cosas que quizá no deberíamos, tomamos decisiones que después entendemos de otra manera, nos hacemos daño incluso cuando hubo cariño y necesitamos tiempo para colocar cada cosa en su sitio. Perdonar no cambia lo que ocurrió ni obliga a reescribir el pasado, pero sí consigue algo extraordinario: que aquello que dolía deje de hacerlo. Eso es lo que hace tan especial aquel abrazo. No borra la historia que hubo entre ellas, la completa. Gemma y Ale no necesitaban volver a ser la pareja que lo ganó todo; bastaba con que fueran capaces de reconocer que todo aquello también merecía ser recordado por las victorias, por el número uno y por todos los momentos que las hicieron tan únicas. Los buenos y los no tan buenos. Quién sabe si se podrá dar ese 'Last Dance' con la camiseta de España. En realidad, poco importa. Porque lo que está claro es que la vida les tenía reservado algo todavía más bonito: mandar un mensaje claro a través de un gesto sincero, improvisado y natural hacia todo el mundo. Sin la pala en la mano, sin una red que les separase. Abrazadas, emocionadas y emocionando a todos. Ese fue el verdadero homenaje, el que nos hicieron estas dos leyendas del pádel. Una instantánea que muchos pueden vislumbrar como el final de una historia. Pero no, amigos y amigas, no lo es. Ese abrazo el principio de otras muchas historias que tomarán ejemplo de esta. El abrazo a la vida, al éxito, al fracaso, al dolor, a la reconciliación. Una historia brutal, imperfecta y humana de la que todos tenemos que aprender. Ojalá.

articles.title: Arsenal vs Chelsea: Gunners stamp authority, but Blues are contenders too
articles.summary: Arsenal’s strong defence and reliable attack edge Chelsea’s bravery and intent in the Premier League’s biggest clash.
articles.body:
Arsenal’s pedigree as defending Premier League champions faced its first big test of the season, with the Gunners hosting title aspirants and big spenders Chelsea on the third matchday.

It is not often that games built up with such hype and expectations live up to their billing, but Arsenal’s 2-1 win over Chelsea certainly delivered on Sunday.

Breathless action , sub-plots galore and a total of 99 minutes and 35 seconds of edge-of-your-seat football drama.

We may only be three rounds into the marathon 38-game Premier League season, but it was the first real test of the credentials for Arsenal and new-look Chelsea after their $473m summer outlay .

Here are five things we learned from the featured clash at the Emirates.

What do you get when you pit arguably the league’s meanest defence against one of its most exciting new attacks? The scoreline might suggest it was a close game, but in reality, it wasn’t.

Chelsea did muster 13 shots on goal, but eight of those came from outside the box, and they combined for an expected goals statistic of 0.35. The Blues had just 25 touches inside the Arsenal penalty area.

Of the 30 Premier League games played among all 20 teams so far, Arsenal have now recorded three of the four lowest totals of expected goals scored against them.

Arsenal’s defensive prowess was even more impressive in the absence of their first-choice defenders William Saliba and Jurrien Timber, who played at least 30 games each in their team’s title-winning run last season. In their absence, defensive options Cristhian Mosquera, Piero Hincapie and Ezri Konsa have all fared admirably.

As a result, Arsenal have won their opening three league games this season while conceding fewer than two goals for the third time ever.

They will hope the omens follow the 2003-04 season, when they finished as unbeaten champions, rather than the 1924-25 season, when they ultimately ended up in 20th.

With young defender Jurrien Timber sidelined following groin surgery, Ben White has filled in at right-back in the opening three games of the campaign. He has also filled Timber’s big attacking boots in addition to keeping things tight at the back.

A whopping 47 percent of Arsenal’s attacks against Chelsea came down the right flank occupied by White and Bukayo Saka.

As busy as Riccardo Calafiori and Christos Tzolis were on the wings, only 28 percent of Arsenal’s attacks came down their left flank, with only 25 percent coming through the middle of the park, occupied by Declan Rice, Myles Lewis-Skelly and Martin Odegaard.

Timber being back in full training and potentially back in action within days is a boost to Mikel Arteta, but White’s form means the Gunners’ manager can afford to take his time in bringing Timber back into the fray.

Only David Raya, Gabriel and White have played more minutes for Arsenal across the opening three games than Kai Havertz.

After back-to-back 90 minutes, the German came off with 12 minutes remaining against Chelsea, allowing Viktor Gyokeres his first minutes of action in the league.

The Swede was heavily linked with a move away from the Emirates in the transfer window, but in the end, teammate Gabriel Jesus made the switch to Barcelona instead, and actually made his debut off the bench at Valencia at the exact same time his former team were hosting Chelsea.

Gyokeres understandably looked rusty; a heavy early touch on the left flank allowed Maxence Lacroix the chance to break up an attack, but he warmed to the task and produced a wonderful flick on halfway to launch another counter.

Meanwhile, Havertz had 10 touches in the opposition box in 78 minutes, the first time he’s reached double figures in a Premier League match since January 2025 – a run of 19 appearances. He also picked up his fourth goal against his former club in nine appearances in league and cup, six of which have now ended in Arsenal wins with the other three drawn.

Havertz clearly wants to keep a grip on his starting forward role.

After a stellar World Cup run with Norway, Arsenal captain Martin Odegaard’s renaissance has continued.

The 27-year-old might have lifted the Premier League trophy last May, but his influence on the season as a whole was far less obvious. He started just 24 Premier League games and played a total of 1,371 minutes – sixth among Gunners midfielders.

His goal against Chelsea was, however, his third in four appearances across all competitions this season – this after netting just once in 36 outings last term – and he once again proved the vital cog in Arsenal’s attack in a Player of the Match performance.

Are Chelsea a force to be reckoned with?

Well, it certainly looks like a step in the right direction. On the evidence of the opening three games, a new-look Chelsea look like top-four contenders once again.

The Blues finished nine places and 33 points adrift of Arsenal last season, but had it not been for a flying David Raya save from Estevao’s rasping late shot, they might have snatched a point at the home of the champions in just their third game under Xabi Alonso.

There are problems for the Spaniard to solve as Chelsea have now gone 19 league games without a clean sheet, and despite the attacking threat of Joao Pedro, Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers, they created an expected goals tally of just 0.35 across 90 minutes.

However, Chelsea fans can be optimistic as they are the first team in Premier League history to score inside the opening five minutes in each of their first three games of the season.

The five-time champions also showed innovation and bravery to nullify the threat of set-piece specialists Arsenal by restricting them to just five corners in total.

The Blues sent four players upfield from their own box before the corner was taken, dragging Arsenal players with them and sending one man out to try and charge down the kick.

Ben White, left, was a standout performer for Arsenal. [Ryan Pierse/Getty Images]
Martin Odegaard scored Arsenal’s second goal. [Tony O Brien/Reuters]
Morgan Rogers celebrates scoring with Joao Pedro. [Tony O Brien/Reuters]

articles.title: Fury claims Joshua fight is off, calls for another Usyk rematch
articles.summary: Tyson Fury says Anthony Joshua is ‘weak-minded’ and cannot make up his mind about the date and venue of their fight.
articles.body:
Tyson Fury claims Anthony Joshua is backing out of their much-anticipated all-British heavyweight boxing showdown and has challenged Oleksandr Usyk to a trilogy fight, throwing the planned Fury-Joshua clash into doubt.

In an expletive-laden video posted on Instagram on Sunday, Fury, 38, claimed Joshua was pulling out of the fight.

Fury and Joshua have been locked in talks over a long-awaited meeting, but the “Gypsy King” is impatient with the lack of confirmation, calling his rival a “coward” last week.

The two former heavyweight world champions were expected to meet in November at Madison Square Garden in New York, but the choice of venue was met with backlash from British boxing fans.

In a string of videos posted over the past week, Fury claimed that Joshua’s lack of response and indecision on the venue have cast doubts over the fight.

He instead asked his longtime Ukrainian rival Usyk to meet him in the ring again .

“This will only lead me to a fight with Oleksandr Usyk,” he said. “Oleksandr, you’re his [Joshua’s] trainer and his sensei, and you know he is … weak-minded … and that he would never fight the Gypsy King, which you have had the guts to do twice.

“You got the decisions last time, fair play to you. Good luck to you; let’s do it again. Let’s run it back in November.

“The ball is now in your court … do you want to fight me this year, 2026, or are you calling it quits? Let me know because I am now looking for a new opponent.”

Fury has twice lost to Usyk , a two-time undisputed heavyweight champion.

Joshua has been working with the Ukrainian’s training team.

Madison Square Garden was widely expected to be announced as the venue for the Fury-Joshua fight, even though Joshua’s camp prefers Wembley Stadium.

articles.title: Cody Rhodes, Bronson Reed, Real Winners and Losers of WWE Sunday Night's Main Event Match Card
articles.summary: WWE's Sunday Night's Main Event match card consisted of five matches and was ultimately a mixed bag of an evening.
articles.body:
WWE's Sunday Night's Main Event match card consisted of five matches and was ultimately a mixed bag of an evening.

Atlanta's own Cody Rhodes squared off against Randy Orton in the main event, and similar to their previous outing at WrestleMania 42, it was a well-wrestled affair with an overbooked finish. One of the two men came across exceptionally poor with the way they were portrayed.

The show also saw Bronson Reed finally make his long-awaited return by aiding Bron Breakker in his battle with Oba Femi. Reed appeared to be in the best shape WWE fans have ever seen him in and received a raucous reaction from the live crowd.

In other action, a new United States champion was crowned and Jade Cargill's crew reigned supreme in six-woman tag team action.

These are the real winners and losers of WWE Sunday Night's Main Event.

No one emerged from Sunday Night's Main Event looking more inept than Baron Corbin.

WWE brought back The Nomad in shocking fashion over the summer and immediately inserted him into the United States Championship picture. Although Corbin regained the gold for the first time in nearly a decade at SummerSlam, it always felt like it was more a matter of when than if Williams would get the belt back.

Sure enough, the two continued to feud going into Sunday Night's Main Event, with it being established that Williams would get a rematch with Corbin for the championship if Lil Yatchy could last five minutes with Corbin.

Predictably, Corbin could have put Yatchy away at any moment but opted not to out of arrogance, which cost him in the end. The subsequent bout between Corbin and Williams was solid and culminated in Corbin's reign ending after just one month.

Despite his surging popularity, Williams wasn't exactly lighting SmackDown's midcard on fire when he last held the star-spangled prize, whereas Corbin could have been booked dominantly as champ until finally being beaten.

Corbin can still be redeemed in the aftermath of the event, but his title run short being cut short certainly makes him a lot less of a threat to the rest of the roster.

Oba Femi vs. Bron Breakker in a battle for the future of WWE was easily the most anticipated outing going into Sunday Night's Main Event. The two had a quality contest that didn't quite meet the lofty expectations had set for it, which is acceptable if the idea is for them to run it back before long.

As underwhelming as the disqualification finish was, it wasn't totally unexpected, nor was the return of Bronson Reed. The Tsunami-splashing destroyer and Breakker took turns attacking Femi to ensure he was left laying.

The bout itself was enjoyable, but Reed by far gained the most from what we got. He reemerged looking leaner and meaning than ever before and almost overshadowed Breakker during that post-match assault on Femi.

All signs point to Femi transitioning into a feud with Reed and that keeping him busy for the foreseeable future, presumably with Femi going over decisively. Although that'd be a waste of Reed's current momentum, it's imperative WWE do what they can to build him up as much as possible before then so the inevitable loss doesn't do as much damage.

Live musical acts and WWE have never gelled well together outside of entrances, yet higher-ups clearly view them as being worthwhile as seen at Sunday Night's Main Event.

WWE had already announced that world-renowned rapper Quavo rapper would be performing an unreleased track to kick off the event. Although it was perfectly fine for what it was, it had no business being on a show with so few matches, as it didn't set the strongest tone for the rest of the night.

It didn't help that it was quickly followed by Lil Yatchy being in action, and although the artist has roots in Georgia, him taking on Baron Corbin wasn't the attraction WWE likely hoped it would be. If anything, the match only made it more apparent that his role has run its course.

There's nothing wrong with mainstream celebrities such as Quavo and Yatchy occasionally appearing for WWE based on their passion for the product, but prioritizing them over others who struggle to land television time sends the wrong message and makes modern-day WWE feel more like a variety show and less like a wrestling show.

The Charlotte Flair vs. Jade Cargill rivalry has been treading water since right before SummerSlam with nothing overly interesting stemming from their segments or matches together.

Tatum Paxley's arrival has added a fun wrinkle to the storyline, but there isn't much of a need for her to continue teaming with Flair and Alexa Bliss beyond their loss at Sunday Night's Main Event. The top takeaway of their otherwise forgettable six-woman tag team match was that Cargill pinned Flair for a much-needed momentum boost.

Prior to Sunday night, Cargill hadn't won a match that mattered since before WrestleMania 42. She failed in back-to-back WWE Women's Championship matches with Rhea Ripley, came up short in the Ladder match for the interim title at SummerSlam and lost her first-ever one-on-one encounter with Flair on the subsequent SmackDown.

Cargill desperately needed to return to her winning ways if a rematch with Flair is going to have any juice. Having her pin Flair herself made it even more meaningful.

Cargill and Flair have been feuding since the spring, so it shouldn't be much longer until they collide again and settle their score so both women can set their sights back on championship gold.

WWE has had a knack this year for putting Cody Rhodes in almost impossible positions where he loses even when he wins.

Of course, the latter wasn't the case at Sunday Night's Main Event as he lost his match to Randy Orton, but the booking surrounding the finish left a lot to be desired.

Much like at WrestleMania 42, Rhodes and Orton again had an above-average encounter. All they needed to do was deliver an ending that was clean and satisfying, but they once again made matters more complicated than they needed to be with ref bumps and a low blow.

Worse yet, Rhodes exhibited heel tendencies by systemically picking apart Orton and hitting him with multiple finishers, only to get tricked by Orton into letting his guard down and eating defeat.

Orton winning was the right call, but giving him the straightforward victory instead of attempting to protect Rhodes at all costs would have been more effective. Rhodes can't be compelling as a character if he isn't allowed to evolve, or at least not be made to look foolish by falling for the same tired tropes as every other babyface.

Graham Mirmina, aka Graham "GSM" Matthews, has specialized in sports and entertainment writing since 2010. Visit his website, WrestleRant , and subscribe to his YouTube channel for more wrestling-related content.

articles.title: WWE Rumors on Roster Releases, New Day's Pay Cut and Royce Keys' 946 Faction
articles.summary: Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe.
articles.body:
Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe.

Lexis King & Former Star Carolina Cruz Get Engaged

WWE recently released 10 talents this past week, but one in particular reportedly caught many by surprise.

According to Wrestling Observer's Bryan Alvarez , Wendy Choo's release blindsided her peers inside the WWE Performance Center.

"Apparently the whole PC was shocked that Wendy Choo was released," Alvarez reported (h/t Steve Carrier of Ringside News).

Choo was the biggest name in WWE's latest batch of roster cuts, most of whom were in the company's developmental system. Choo was an NXT veteran who debuted in 2018, and she claimed her first title in her WWE career when she won the Evolve Women's Championship earlier this year. Her 70-day title reign ended over the summer with a loss to Nikkita Lyons.

In addition to her recent push inside the ring, Choo also appeared on WWE LFG as a player-coach, working with younger talents vying for a developmental contract.

It's clear that Choo had the respect of those who worked with her, so she should have no trouble getting opportunities to continue her wrestling career in other promotions.

New Details on New Day's Rumored WWE Pay Cut

After rumors surfaced that Kofi Kingston and Austin Creed were asked by WWE to take a 75 percent pay cut, it now sounds like that figure is a bit exaggerated.

During an episode of Grilling JR , Conrad Thompson claimed that Kingston and Creed, who performed as New Day in WWE and are now known as New Level in AEW, were asked to give up 75 percent of their pay in their new deal before they ultimately turned down the offer and parted ways with the company.

However, Bryan Alvarez debunked that report while speaking on Wrestling Observer Live , saying the requested pay cut was similar to what other former WWE Superstars have seen.

"There was a story that The New Level were told to take a 75 percent pay cut. That is not the number," Alvarez said (h/t Felix Upton of Ringside News). "I was told by people who know these guys that it was just over 50 percent. Ridge Holland just happened to come out and announce his requested pay cut was 56 percent, and that is exactly what The New Level was asked to take—56 percent, just over 50 percent."

During an appearance on The Ariel Helwani Show last week, Kingston confirmed that he and Creed were asked to take a pay cut of "more than 50 percent." He added that it was clear the duo didn't feel the proposed terms reflected their contributions to the company.

"We just thought that the terms that they wanted us to perform under were not fair based on what we brought to the table, based on what we're worth, based on the knowledge and prowess that we have as performers, as wrestlers, what we can give back to younger people, what we do from a point of entertainment," Kingston said.

It sounds like Royce Keys had more control over the formation of his new 946 faction than initially realized.

According to a recent report from False Finish (h/t Steve Carrier of Ringside News), sources said that Keys hand-picked OTM's Bronco Nima and Lucien Price out of NXT to join him on the main roster in his feud against Jacob Fatu and The Bloodline. The report also noted that Keys will be presented as the sole leader of the group, with Nima and Price operating under him.

Per Carrier , False Finish also reported that sources said there is a possibility that another member could eventually be added to 946. The current lineup is expected to remain intact for the time being, but WWE could expand the group once it gets more established.

WWE has already filmed promotional material explaining the faction's origins, and the trio recently shot vignettes in Orlando to provide more background.

It was previously reported that OTM's move to Monday Night Raw alongside Keys received positive reactions, so it sounds like the group is positioned for some major opportunities going forward.

articles.title: Way-Too-Early 2026-27 Calder Trophy Rankings for NHL Rookie of the Year
articles.summary: Any preseason NHL award ranking should be taken with a grain of salt, but none more than the Calder Trophy.
articles.body:
Any preseason NHL award ranking should be taken with a grain of salt, but none more than the Calder Trophy.

You may think, going into the season, that there's an obvious answer. Most years—not all, but most—that obvious answer will be wrong.

There are so many variables involved beyond just "who is purely the best rookie player." What does your team's roster makeup look like, and how will that affect playing time? Are there other rookies on the team to split the vote or the opportunities? Does your team suck even though you're really good?

And the worst of the bunch: Did you get injured at any point in your rookie season, thus robbing you of games played and opportunities to rack up points?

So let's look at the playing field and where things stand in a vacuum. We'll check back in later in the season to see how on track we were.

5. Roman Kantserov, LW/RW, Chicago Blackhawks

Chicago Blackhawks rookie forward Roman Kantserov is perhaps the biggest question mark of our top five. We know that he's an unbelievable offensive player; Kantserov had the most goals in the KHL last season with 36, and was ninth overall in scoring with 64 points. Ten of those 36 goals were power-play goals, enough to show that he's capable of being a power-play asset, but not so many that he's only or primarily scoring on the power play.

What we don't know is how his game will translate to North American hockey. It's always a learning curve, moving from any European league to the NHL, though the KHL is one of the better leagues for predicting translatable scoring ability. It'll be interesting to see who he ends up playing with in Chicago as well. Young Blackhawks star Connor Bedard seems the most likely option for a linemate, but it's possible he ends up alongside fellow rookie Anton Frondell. With Frondell being another dark-horse Calder candidate, just outside the top five that we discuss here, that could backfire on both players as far as the hunt for the rookie of the year award goes.

Pretty good as far as linemates and teammates go, though.

Winning the Calder Trophy as a defenseman is an uphill battle, but it can be done. Just ask last year's winner, Matthew Schaefer, or this player's brother, Lane Hutson. But Cole Hutson is not Lane Hutson, and this season's Washington Capitals are not the 2024-25 Montreal Canadiens.

Without question, Cole Hutson has the talent necessary to win the Calder in a vacuum. He's extremely skilled, with excellent vision, deception, and puck-distribution skills. He's clearly capable of translating the offense he brought to teams at lower levels of hockey to the NHL. Unfortunately for Hutson, the season isn't played in a vacuum.

He's got a lot stacked against him in this Calder race: the players he's up against, the structure of the Washington Capitals roster, which defines his opportunities, and the aforementioned fact that it's just harder for defensemen to stand out in the needed ways in general. John Carlson leaving the Capitals could create special teams opportunities for Hutson, which would push the Calder door open a bit further. Watch this space, because he could definitely end up a dark horse option.

3. Ivar Stenberg, LW/RW, San Jose Sharks

This is a 2A-2B situation, for sure—I think there's an equal chance at the Calder for Martone and the San Jose Sharks' second-overall pick, Ivar Stenberg. And with the question marks currently in the ether for Gavin McKenna, we'll likely have a better idea next time we check in whether that Martone-Stenberg combo will leapfrog McKenna or not.

There's no question that Stenberg is the more complete player of the two, with experience playing men's professional hockey under his belt and a reputation for being trusted anywhere on the ice. He's almost certainly going to get power-play time from the get-go, though which unit remains to be seen, and that could be a difference-maker.

The problem is that the Calder often turns into a points contest, and while we definitely can't rule out Stenberg passing Martone and McKenna in that area, we also don't feel strongly that he will. The Sharks have quite the cadre of skilled young players, and sometimes that plays out poorly for a rookie seeking that Calder opportunity. Which leads to another question we await the answer to: who will Stenberg play alongside? That itself will shape both how his offensive game and how his perception around the league play out.

2. Porter Martone, RW, Philadelphia Flyers

You may be surprised by this second-ranked player; then again, if you've seen him play, you might not be. Porter Martone is an offensive wrecking ball on his best days. If he plays the way we know that he's capable of, and scores the way we know he's capable of, he almost feels like more of a shoo-in than McKenna. At the very least, he's going to put up a serious fight for that top spot. He had 10 points, including four goals, in his first nine regular-season NHL games, which he swiftly followed with five points in his first 10 playoff games. It was a "sit up and take notice" kind of moment.

That being said, Martone has that same off-puck engagement question as McKenna. He did go a long way toward assuaging that concern toward the end of last season, and if other Flyers can pick up the slack in that area, it may not be a major issue. But it's something worth keeping an eye on. He is going to have to play less to the perimeter than he's used to in order to sustain his offensive production across an 84-game season. We have less of a worry about him adjusting to the pace, given how many games he played last season and the variety of environments he played in.

Even with his foibles in mind, it will not be surprising in the least if Martone pulls off a Calder Trophy win. Especially given how he kicked off his NHL career at the end of last season.

1. Gavin McKenna, LW, Toronto Maple Leafs

Our 2026 first overall pick feels like the obvious answer.

We're ranking him first here because he's the best option in terms of pure skill—McKenna's offensive instincts are off-the-rails good, particularly the way that he is able to process the flow of the game.

He's an incredible playmaker, able to accurately connect passes that others wouldn't even think to make. His linemates will most likely include at least one of Auston Matthews, William Nylander, or John Tavares. It's a good spot to be in for one of the NHL's most anticipated rookies of the last several years.

But there are also many unanswered questions that could trip him up.

Are the Leafs going to be any good? Couldn't tell you. But McKenna wouldn't be the first Calder candidate to lose out on the trophy because his team laid a giant egg. If they are good, however, and he's getting offensive opportunities left and right, his own issues off the puck might offset the pros of his game. He also has to adjust to what is now an 84-game season.

We still think he's the most likely candidate now, before any games have been played. Time to watch how those games go.

articles.title: Pakistan captain Fatima Sana fined over Shafali Verma gesture in Asia Cup
articles.summary: Sana gestured towards the pavilion after removing Verma in a caught-and-bowled dismissal in their Asia Cup match.
articles.body:
Pakistan captain Fatima Sana has been sanctioned by the International Cricket Council (ICC) for gesturing during her team’s Asia Cup group match against India last week.

Sana was fined 10 percent of her match fee by the ICC on Monday, two days after India handed Pakistan a record T20 defeat in the regional tournament.

The incident occurred after Sana caught and bowled out Shafali Verma in her second over and gestured to the pavilion. Verma scored 12 runs off six balls as India beat Pakistan by seven wickets to remain unbeaten in the competition.

Sana admitted to her offence, which breached Article 2.5 of the ICC Code of Conduct relating to “using language, actions or gestures which disparage or which could provoke an aggressive reaction from a batter upon dismissal”.

Additionally, one demerit point was added to her disciplinary record for her second offence in 24 months. The previous incident occurred during a T20I against Ireland in August 2025.

According to the ICC’s Code of Conduct, Level 1 breaches carry a minimum penalty of an official reprimand, a maximum penalty of 50 percent of a player’s match fee and one or two demerit points.

India have cruised through to the semifinals with six points from three matches. Pakistan are looking for a win against Hong Kong on Monday.

The 50-over world champions have won a record seven Asia Cup titles, most recently in 2022.

Pakistan have never won the title and have twice finished runners-up to neighbours India, in 2012 and 2016.

Sana was named Pakistan’s captain in October 2024, becoming the youngest player to lead the women’s cricket team at the age of 22.

articles.title: Harry Kane opens up on Ballon d’Or hopes after eclipsing Cristiano Ronaldo goal record
articles.summary: Kane scored 73 times for club and country last season and is the bookmakers’ favourite to win the Ballon d’Or
articles.body:
Following a remarkably prolific campaign, Harry Kane has expressed his delight at being in contention for the Ballon d'Or , describing himself as "extremely proud" of his achievement.

The 33-year-old is the bookmakers' favourite to collect the honour in October after scoring 73 goals for club and country last term, beating Cristiano Ronaldo 's career-best single-season record of 69 set in 2011-12, and only being surpassed by Lionel Messi 's record 82 goals from the same season.

Should Kane claim the prize, he would become just the fifth Englishman to receive it, following Sir Stanley Matthews, Sir Bobby Charlton , Kevin Keegan and Michael Owen, and the first since Owen's success in 2001.

In an interview with Owen Hargreaves for TNT Sports , the Bayern Munich striker said: "I'm extremely proud of the season I put up, for sure.

"Not that long ago, I was that fan wanting to become a professional footballer and I am here now and winning awards and the Ballon d'Or is the same.

"Of course, now it is out of my hands, it is down to the voters and the people who decide it. The season I had was my best season by far and we'll have to wait and see."

Kane is yet to score in the Bundesliga this term across Bayern's opening two fixtures, which featured a 5-1 win over Stuttgart and a goalless draw against Schalke.

Yet despite his historic output last season, he remains driven to raise his standards.

He added: "It is a weird one because I am already focused on this season now and the next season. Can I be better? Can I improve? But I also want to appreciate what I did.

"The thing with football opinions – there are so many opinions, so many arguments for different players and people love this player because he's fast and he's got great IQ and his finishing is great.

"So I think that is what makes football special, all those debates, and the Ballon d'Or is definitely one of them. I'm happy that I am in contention."

The England captain admitted to being "amazed" to find his name alongside Messi and Ronaldo, two figures widely considered the game's greatest ever.

He added: "I grew up watching Messi and Ronaldo, the era of them just dominating and dominating.

"Obviously Messi is the only one to have scored more with 82, but even some of their other seasons, and Ronaldo's highest I think was 69.

"These are numbers that I just thought were silly, which they are. They are the two greatest of our generation and arguably of all time. So 73 goals, even for me, I am pretty amazed by that."

articles.title: New Williams handball footage emerges
articles.summary: New video footage has been released that shows the ball coming off Neco Williams' arm in the lead-up to his disallowed goal in the 0-0 draw against Tottenham...
articles.body:
New video footage has been released that shows the ball coming off Neco Williams' arm in the lead-up to his disallowed goal in the 0-0 draw against Tottenham Hotspur .

The Nottingham Forest defender bundled the ball home in the 67th minute but video assistant referee Peter Bankes stepped in to rule out the goal for accidental handball.

Williams and Forest manager Oliver Glasner were adamant after the match that there was no proof the ball touched an arm.

While the footage vindicates the VAR's decision, it may not end the arguments about the decision to rule out the goal.

The new camera angle was not one of those available to Bankes during the game - so it is unlikely to end the anger from Forest fans over the validity of the intervention, even if we know the VAR was ultimately correct.

On the new footage, Williams touches the ball with his left arm then his right forearm before it goes into the net.

The VAR hub only has access to the broadcast cameras, and this camera was one of several which does not transmit as part of match coverage.

Bankes believed the proof on the angles he had available came from the ripple of Williams' shirt as the ball touched his right forearm.

BBC Sport understands that Pro Ref - the new name for the refereeing body that was previously called Professional Game Match Officials (PGMO) - is completely happy with the decision to rule out the goal.

There is irritation within Pro Ref about how the story has developed, partly because Williams was so unequivocal that the ball had not touched his arm - when there is now evidence to the contrary.

"I've seen the images and the replays and at not one moment did I think I handballed it," Williams told Sky Sports.

"I have seen all the images and at not one moment can you tell that has clearly hit my arms, because it never. I knew straight away I've headed it down in between my arms. It didn't hit my arm."

The feeling is that if Williams had not been so certain with his comments that the criticism would not have been as strong.

articles.title: 49ers' Australia trip may be a logistical nightmare for a few players
articles.summary: Weeks is the only snapper on the team, but he was released just before the August 30th deadline to trim down to the 53-man active roster
articles.body:
Imagine prepping for the trip to Melbourne, Australia, for the San Francisco 49ers to face the Los Angeles Rams on Thursday. Then being cut and sent back home before playing a snap. That's exactly what happened to 49ers tight end Brayden Willis on Saturday to make room for long snapper Jon Weeks, who was promoted to the active roster.

Weeks is the only snapper on the team, but he was released just before the August 30th deadline to trim down to the 53-man active roster, leaving the 49ers with zero long snappers. Weeks was, however, added to the practice squad.

Brayden Willis, on the other hand, will hit the waiver wire. It is not yet known whether he has left the country, but if another team claims him, he will have to quickly board a plane and make the trek across the pond back to the States. Reports close to the team have indicated that he could be signed to the 49ers' practice squad and remain with them while in Australia.

The move could mean that 49ers tight end George Kittle is completely healthy after suffering from a torn Achilles tendon back in January. The trip to Australia could turn out to be a logistical nightmare for a few players, as the 49ers also claimed Khalid Kareem off the Atlanta Falcons' practice squad, meaning he will have to make the 21-hour trip to Australia.

articles.title: Do the Washington Commanders have a path to 8-plus wins in 2026?
articles.summary: How many wins will the Commanders have in 2026?
articles.body:
How many games will the Washington Commanders win in 2026? Well, it depends on who you ask.

When the Commanders signed wide receiver Stefon Diggs last month, there was genuine excitement about the upcoming season. Then, right after, star left tackle Laremy Tunsil tore his triceps, and reports of Washington's struggles in training camp to protect quarterback Jayden Daniels led some to think the Commanders would be terrible in 2026.

In recent weeks, several analysts have predicted doom for Washington in 2026. It's apparently the new popular take among NFL analysts who don't follow the team closely.

CBS Sports recently predicted whether the Commanders will finish over or under 7.5 wins. DraftKings Sportsbook set the 7.5-win line for 2026.

Pereles: Under 7.5 (-125). Things were looking up for a potential bounce-back year before Laremy Tunsil and others got hurt, and the lack of top-end talent and depth got exposed. Jayden Daniels should thrive in David Blough's new system, and Washington is hoping both Blough's and defensive coordinator Daronte Jones' schemes make the sum greater than the parts. But Washington faces a brutal schedule and simply has too many holes at crucial positions, such as offensive line and cornerback.

Nothing Pereles said here was egregiously wrong. The Tunsil injury hurt. Fortunately, Washington has Brandon Coleman, who manned the position as a rookie two seasons ago. No one is Tunsil, but Coleman played well there as a rookie, and should only be better now. The problem for Washington's offensive line is at center. Can Nick Allegretti reward GM Adam Peters' faith in him? And if he does, can he stay healthy? He missed almost all of training camp, exposing the Commanders' scary lack of depth on the interior.

There is a lot to like about Washington. You have Daniels, the best collection of offensive weapons he's had since entering the NFL—and a faster and improved defense. If the Commanders can remain relatively healthy, the defense will be better. Yes, there are still concerns at corner, but Daronte Jones' scheme is built on pressure that should help the secondary.

But yes, the first part of Washington's schedule is brutal. If the Commanders can somehow go 3-3 in their first six games, then they'll have a good shot at returning to the playoffs. However, if they win fewer than three of those games, it could be a long season.

The Commanders may be the NFL's most mysterious team heading into Week 1.

articles.title: Barcelona legend Iniesta plays down comparisons between him and Pedri: ‘He has his own story’
articles.summary: Barcelona now boast one of the world’s most dangerous midfield combinations after the signing of Rodri, as they have the Spanish national team captain linkin...
articles.body:
Barcelona now boast one of the world's most dangerous midfield combinations after the signing of Rodri, as they have the Spanish national team captain linking up with Pedri, one of football's greatest anomalies.

The one game Pedri and Rodri started together last night made it clear that they are capable of achieving great things, for the veteran unlocked the Canary Islander and enabled him to play in a more advanced position.

With freedom to roam in the final third and link up with the attackers at the edge of the box, Pedri's role was very reminiscent of Andres Iniesta's role when Sergio Busquets and Xavi took care of the defensive responsibilities.

Barcelona legend Andres Iniesta opened up on Pedri's style of play and impact on the team's performances over the years.

"He is a player who, when you watch him on television, amazes you with what he does, and with how easy, simple and natural he makes it look," Iniesta began, showering high praise on Pedri.

One of the world's best players. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images)

The legend was then asked if the Barcelona midfielder was closer to him or Xavi Hernandez, to which he said

"[He is] not a mixture of anything because he has his own qualities, his strengths and his own things to continue developing and improving."

"He is a very young player, although he is already very decisive for Barça and the national team," he added.

Speaking on the Canary Islander's journey up the ranks to elite football, Iniesta said

"Pedri is an extraordinary footballer. I love him because behind him is a story full of hard work and overcoming difficulties. And above all, he has his own story."

Iniesta is Pedri's idol. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images)

In all his interviews thus far, Pedri has always maintained that Iniesta was his role model growing up.

"For him to say that I was his childhood idol is something beautiful. He watched the way I played. To be a reference for someone—who wouldn't like to hear something like that?," Iniesta remarked when asked about the same.

Towards the end of his interview, the Barcelona legend was asked what Pedri must do to become as great as him.

"Pedri doesn't have to be me. He has to be Pedri, with his own characteristics, building his own path. That is the most valuable thing for any person: being yourself. And that is what he is."

Elaborating on what makes him a different player with a special talent, the former Barcelona midfielder said

"Above all, he is a difference-maker, capable of creating plays that didn't exist before."

"He comes up with passes that nobody had seen previously because he possesses tremendous talent," he added.

Finally, Iniesta concluded his opinion on Pedri with a simple, yet powerful praise.

articles.title: Marotta Holds the Key to Calhanoglu’s Inter Future
articles.summary: Hakan Calhanoglu remains as central to Inter as ever, but his contract situation is still unresolved with the Turkish midfielder’s deal running only until th...
articles.body:
Hakan Calhanoglu remains as central to Inter as ever, but his contract situation is still unresolved with the Turkish midfielder's deal running only until the summer of 2027, and the next move now rests with Giuseppe Marotta rather than the player.

According to TUTTOmercatoWEB , journalist Marco Conterio frames the situation as a stand-off in which Calhanoglu 's willingness to stay is obvious, but formal renewal discussions have not yet taken place. Marotta has said Inter will soon begin consulting agents to establish what their players want, adding that a demonstrated sense of belonging should be respected when evaluating whether to continue a relationship.

There is no debating Calhanoglu's importance to this Inter side. His personality, his standing in the dressing room and his quality on the pitch have all been on display again at the start of this season, whether starting or coming off the bench, with his recent contribution underlining why the club cannot afford to let this drag.

Christian Chivu has even managed his minutes carefully, partly to preserve him for Wednesday's Champions League test against Real Madrid. Calhanoglu himself has downplayed speculation linking him to a return to Turkey, insisting instead that his focus is on meriting a new contract that, as things stand, has not yet been discussed by either side.

Marotta's promised consultation with agents will need to cover more than just Calhanoglu. Federico Dimarco and Carlos Augusto are among others whose futures hinge on similar conversations, and how Inter structures its approach to contract renewals this autumn will say plenty about Marotta's broader strategy heading into the business end of the season.

articles.title: Tyson Fury suggests fight with Joshua is off and challenges Usyk to trilogy bout instead
articles.summary: Tyson Fury has indicated his long-awaited fight with Anthony Joshua is off and challenged Oleksandr Usyk to a trilogy bout in November instead.  Negotiations...
articles.body:
LONDON (AP) — Tyson Fury has indicated his long-awaited fight with Anthony Joshua is off and challenged Oleksandr Usyk to a trilogy bout in November instead.

Negotiations for a lucrative all-British fight between former heavyweight champions Fury and Joshua have dragged on without a firm date or venue, and key financial questions left open.

In a video packed with insults and expletives on Instagram late Sunday, Fury laid the blame with Joshua, branding him "weak-minded" and suggesting he lacked the courage to take the fight. "This will only lead me to a fight with Oleksandr Usyk," Fury said.

The Ukrainian vacated his three heavyweight world titles in June and said he wanted one "last dance" fight before retirement.

"You got the decisions last time, fair play to you. Good luck to you, well, let's do it again. Let's run it back in November. The ball is now in your court, Oleksandr," Fury added. "Do you want to fight me this year, 2026, or are you calling quits? Let me know because I am now looking for a new opponent."

Usyk (25-0) became the first undisputed world heavyweight champion in 24 years when he beat Fury by decision in May 2024, and he outpointed the British fighter again in their rematch seven months later.

Fury (36-2-1) and Joshua (30-4) both won tuneup fights in July that were expected to be a prelude to their all-British bout, though Joshua came near to a shock loss when he was knocked down twice by Kristian Prenga.

Usyk, too, looked short of his best in his stoppage win over Rico Verhoeven, a Dutch kickboxer fighting as a boxer for just the second time, in May.

The Atlanta Falcons have named Tua Tagovailoa as the starting quarterback for their Week 1 matchup against the Pittsburgh Steelers at Acrisure Stadium, the team announced on Monday morning.

Tagovailoa has passed for 18,166 yards, 120 touchdowns and 59 interceptions over six NFL seasons with the Miami Dolphins. Despite a promising start in Miami, Tagovailoa's career took a turn after he sustained multiple serious concussions. Tua lost his job late in the 2025 season and was released back in March.

Atlanta signed Tagovailoa to a one-year deal for the veteran minimum. The Falcons had him battle Michael Penix Jr. for the starting gig throughout training camp. However, the team did not clarify if the move was for the entire season, but we at least know who will start the season opener.

We're not sure what it means for Penix, who was just cleared for contact about two weeks ago. Penix has passed for 2,757 yards, 12 passing touchdowns, and 6 interceptions in 14 career games (12 starts). He had an up-and-down season in 2025 - his first as a starter - but he was playing great against the eventual NFC South-champion Carolina Panthers in Week 11 before tearing his ACL.

The Falcons will open against the Steelers on the road in Week 1, meaning they'll face four-time league MVP Aaron Rodgers. For now at least, it appears to be Tagovailoa's team.
