The biggest question facing the 2026 Atlanta Falcons has been answered.

On Monday, the Falcons announced that Tua Tagovailoa, who signed with the Falcons this offseason after being released by the Miami Dolphins, has been named the starter for Week 1 against the Steelers in Pittsburgh .

The Falcons' quarterback situation has been a roller-coaster ride since the first day of training camp — and not a particularly fun one.

On Day 1 of camp, the team announced that Trevor Siemian had been released with an injury settlement; Tua Tagovailoa would not be participating in practice due to some lower back stiffness; and the team was signing QB Cooper Rush. Michael Penix Jr. wasn't medically cleared until the final week of training camp, so that left Rush and rookie undrafted free agent Jack Strand to participate in that first practice.

Stefanski declined to name a starter throughout the preseason, even though Penix's medical clearance came so late in the process that he was unable to take any preseason game snaps.

And Tua's preseason performance didn't necessarily enthuse fans. He completed 3 of 5 attempts for 22 yards, zero touchdowns, and zero picks in Week 1 of the preseason against the Broncos, sat out Week 2 (this was always Stefanski's plan, to let the starters take most of the joint practice reps with the Colts and sit out that preseason game), and went 7 of 8 for 95 yards, no touchdowns, no picks, and one absurd botched snap that turned into a fumble and kind of overshadowed the rest of his performance.

But I have concerns about whether or not Michael Penix is ready, after basically three days of full practice, to play an entire NFL game. I do believe, based on what Penix has said about it, he's past the mental aspect of his recovery, and I trust that he's physically healthy. I worry that his lack of contact leading up to Week 1 could lead to a different injury altogether, or that the lack of contact and full-speed practice or preseason action has him unprepared for the speed of the regular-game.

And that's not to suggest there aren't injury concerns with Tua. His concussion history worries me — not because of football, but for the sake of his long-term health and well being. But he has gotten most of the meaningful work this preseason with the starters, he has participated fully in padded practices, joint practices, and the preseason, and it stands to reason that he is more prepared — through no fault of Penix's, just because of the timing of his medical clearance — to be the Week 1 starter.

Tua spent the first six seasons of his career with the Miami Dolphins, who drafted him with the fifth overall pick out of Alabama in the 2020 NFL Draft. He has a 68% completion percentage over his NFL career, throwing 120 touchdowns against 59 interceptions.

He was released by the Dolphins in March 2026 after a 2025 season he finished with 2,660 yards, 20 touchdowns, 15 picks, and took 30 sacks. He was benched for the final three games of the season, and the Falcons took advantage of him being cut to sign him for an extremely affordable one-year deal. New head coach Kevin Stefanski and general manager Ian Cunningham saw him as competition and insurance for Penix, and now he is the starter.

I don't think this decision says anything about either Tua's or Penix's long-term future with the Falcons or as the starter. There's a lot of football to be played before I'll have an opinion about that.

But I do think it's Tua's job to lose. If he goes out there and balls out, it would be silly to sit him. If he doesn't, though, it likely won't be long before Penix is ready to step in.

Can the 2026 version of Tua Tagovailoa do that, and stay healthy? That's now one of the biggest questions facing the 2026 Falcons now.

articles.title: Joe Morgan, two-time division-winning manager for Red Sox, dies at 95
articles.summary: Joe Morgan, who managed the Boston Red Sox to the 1988 American League East championship, died Sept. 5, the club announced. He was 95.
articles.body:
Joe Morgan, who spent 18 years in the Boston Red Sox organization as a manager, coach and scout and guided them to the 1988 American League East championship, died Saturday, Sept. 5, the club announced Sunday.

Morgan, a Walpole, Massachusetts, native who played at Boston College, managed the Red Sox from 1988-1991, taking over for the fired John McNamara at midseason. The Red Sox were 43-42 at the All-Star break and nine games out of first place when Morgan took over.

He guided them to a 46-31 record and an improbable East title behind pitchers Roger Clemens and Bruce Hurst, who each won 18 games; Clemens led the majors with 291 strikeouts. The Red Sox were swept 4-0 in the AL Championship Series by the Oakland Athletics.

"Joe Morgan holds a special place in Red Sox history," said Red Sox Principal Owner John Henry in a statement released by the team. "When he took over in 1988, he changed the course of a season and created one of the most memorable chapters in the history of this club. The two division titles that followed only strengthened a bond with Red Sox fans that endured for the rest of his life. We extend our deepest condolences to his family and all who loved him."

Added chairman Tom Werner: "'Morgan Magic' is forever part of Red Sox lore. Joe took over in 1988 and gave New England a summer it would never forget. How fitting that, in his final season watching the Red Sox, he saw another team respond to adversity with a remarkable run of its own."

Morgan won 83, 88 and 84 games in his three full seasons managing the club, guiding them to the East title in 1990 before another postseason elimination by Oakland. He was fired shortly after the 1991 season and replaced by Butch Hobson.

Morgan was the longtime manager of the Pawtucket Red Sox , leading the team from 1974 to 1982, and compiling a record of 601-658 through nine seasons, where he helped future Red Sox stars such as Jim Rice, Wade Boggs, Rich Gedman, Fred Lynn and more. He was named International League Manager of the Year in 1977.

The Boston Red Sox re-assigned him as a scout for the 1983 and '84 seasons before he joined the major league team as the first base coach in 1985.

An infielder, Morgan played in 88 major league games with the Milwaukee Braves (1959), Kansas City Athletics (1959), Philadelphia Phillies (1960), Cleveland Indians (1960-61), and St. Louis Cardinals (1964) and began his minor league managerial career in 1966. He is a member of both the Boston Red Sox and Pawtucket Red Sox halls of fame.

articles.title: Falcons pick Tua Tagovailoa as their Week 1 starting quarterback
articles.summary: Six days before the season opener, the Falcons have finally made their choice.
articles.body:
Falcons quarterback Tua Tagovailoa will start on Sunday against the Steelers.

The Falcons finally made the choice today, just six days before the start of the regular season, according to multiple reports.

Tagovailoa was the favorite all along, but Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski declined to make the choice official. Tagovailoa was seemingly competing with Michael Penix for the job, but Penix is coming off a torn ACL last season and wasn't healthy enough to make it a real competition.

The Falcons kept four quarterbacks on the 53-player roster, with Cooper Rush and Jack Strand in the quarterback room along with Tagovailoa and Penix. It's unknown at this point who will be No. 2 on Sunday.

Sunday's game will mark Tagovailoa's second straight game in Pittsburgh, as it was also the site of his last game with the Dolphins, a 28-15 loss after which he was benched for the rest of the season.

Tagovailoa will hope he has more job stability as the starting quarterback in Atlanta, but he might not: Given how long it took Stefanski to make Tagovailoa the starter, he might decide quickly to move on if Tagovailoa isn't working out.

articles.title: Liam Scales delivers verdict on ‘harsh’ and ‘accidental’ St Mirren penalty call
articles.summary: Liam Scales believes the penalty awarded against him in Celtic’s 2-1 victory over St Mirren was “harsh” after an eventful night for the Hoops defender in Pai...
articles.body:
Liam Scales believes the penalty awarded against him in Celtic's 2-1 victory over St Mirren was "harsh" after an eventful night for the Hoops defender in Paisley.

Martin O'Neill's side fell behind in the first half when Chris Mochrie's effort struck Scales' right arm inside the penalty area, with referee Ryan Lee pointing to the spot.

Nikolas Agrafiotis converted to give the hosts the lead, but Scales went from villain to hero after the break by glancing home Celtic's equaliser on 51 minutes before Hyun-jun Yang completed the turnaround shortly afterwards.

"The captain and manager spoke at half-time and we knew we had to get better in the second half," Scales told Sky Sports post-match. "We improved and that paid off after the break as got the goals and the points.

"My own night? It was up and down wasn't it?

"It was accidental for the penalty but I thought it was harsh. Maybe my arm was too high but I have to see it back. I was just relieved to get the goal and get the win."

The victory maintained Celtic's perfect domestic start and moved them five points clear of St Mirren at the Premiership summit.

O'Neill admitted his side had been second best for a spell during a difficult opening half but was pleased with the response after the interval.

articles.title: Nottinghamshire add Hay as Verreynne replacement
articles.summary: Nottinghamshire sign New Zealand wicketkeeper-batter Mitchell Hay to replace Kyle Verreynne for the remainder of the season.
articles.body:
Nottinghamshire have signed New Zealand wicketkeeper-batter Mitchell Hay to replace Kyle Verreynne for the remainder of the season.

Hay, 26, arrives just two days after Verreynne had his latest stint at Trent Bridge cut short when recalled by Cricket South Africa at the weekend.

Notts' director of cricket Mick Newell said losing Verreynne with three County Championship games left to try to retain the Division One title was "not ideal".

Head coach Peter Moores echoed the sentiment of "disappointment" about the loss but, in announcing Hay's arrival, declared the Black Caps international as a "hugely exciting" and "quality" successor.

"He is a mature keeper with the ability to bat in the top six, which fits the role we need coming into the business end of the season," Moores told the club website.

Hay, who has spent his domestic cricket career playing for Canterbury in New Zealand, joins a Notts side that are second in the table and just four points adrift of leaders Somerset.

He has so far scored more than 2,100 first-class runs, with a strike average of 45.14, across his career.

articles.title: Bold Prediction: The Athletic says Cowboys $32M acquisition to reach key metric
articles.summary: The Cowboys didn't have a central figure for the pass rush last season. Do they have one now?
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys used to have a feared pass rush. It might not have been great during the playoffs, but it wasn't that long ago when the team had a top edge-rushing duo reeking havoc on opposing offenses. In 2024, Micah Parsons notched his fourth-straight double-digit sack season, racking up 52.5 sacks in his first four seasons. After his trade to Green Bay, Dallas struggled to convert pressures into sacks, not having anyone capable of capitalizing on their backfield excursions.

The team hopes to have better fortune, thanks to a couple offseason additions and a more creative defensive scheme, designed by new defensive coordinator Christian Parker. After signing the 34-year old in January, Dallas also went out and grabbed Marcus Dixon to coach the defensive line and BT Jordan to coach the pass rushers. Then, when it came to build the roster, they began by trading for Rashan Gary, formerly of the same Packers whom Parsons was sent to.

Gary came with a middle-of-the-road price tag, $32 million over two seasons, but with a reputation as a middle-of-the-road skillset. That doesn't necessarily mean Dallas will only get middle-of-the-road production. In fact, in The Athletic's article on Bold Predictions for each of the 32 NFL teams , Gary gets the Cowboys' honor with a prediction of attaining double-digit sacks.

Gary's career high is 9.5 sacks in 2021. He had 7.5 each of the last two seasons in Green Bay. He has looked like an extremely motivated player throughout training camp, getting as much pressure as any Dallas edge rusher. And the opportunities should be there with an interior defensive line that includes Quinnen Williams and Kenny Clark. Gary and Donovan Ezeiruaku are the expected starters at outside linebacker. Von Miller and rookie Malachi Lawrence should see a lot of opportunities behind them. If Gary, 28, stays healthy, he has a chance to have a big year in Christian Parker's new defensive scheme. — Jon Machota

The 2025 Cowboys were paced by Jadeveon Clowney's 8.5 sacks, but 4.5 of those came in the final two games of the season, after Dallas was already eliminated from the playoffs. If Gary can reach a meaningful, double-digit number, it will likely mean much better results for the team's defense, which will mean much better results for the team as a whole.

Dallas ranked 32nd in starting field position last season . More sacks should equate to more turnovers and punts for opposing teams, and should set up Dak Prescott and the offense with better opportunities. If Gary can spearhead that campaign, it will be a fourth-round pick that wa well worth it.

articles.title: Tony Dorigo drops in on Ups and Downs Cafe
articles.summary: The Leeds United Foundation's Ups and Downs Café takes place on Wednesday afternoons at Elland Road, providing a welcoming and supportive space for supporter...
articles.body:
The Leeds United Foundation's Ups and Downs Café takes place on Wednesday afternoons at Elland Road, providing a welcoming and supportive space for supporters to come together, connect, and share their experiences.

One session in particular was made extra special by a surprise visit from former Leeds United player and Club Ambassador Tony Dorigo. Tony spent time with the group discussing his journey from Australia to the Premier League and his experiences, offering honest and engaging reflections on his career in the game.

He shared memorable stories from his time at Leeds United, including his journey into the professional game, moments that clearly resonated with those in attendance. Tony also welcomed questions from the group, further engaging attendees with an honest look into the former full-backs life in football.

The open discussion allowed supporters to ask questions, reminisce, and hear first-hand accounts of key moments in the club's history from someone who lived them. The session highlighted the power of shared memories and the strong bond between players, managers, and supporters.

The Ups and Downs Café is funded by the Premier League Players Fund and gives attendees the opportunity to visit Elland Road each week in a relaxed and friendly environment. The sessions support mental wellbeing by reducing isolation, encouraging conversation, and creating meaningful social connections.

One of the key benefits of the group is the chance to share stories with people who have lived those experiences together, whether as players, managers, or lifelong supporters. Bringing together supporters, players, and managers in this way strengthens community ties and reinforces the positive impact football can have beyond the pitch.

articles.title: 5 key takeaways from Big Ten football after Week 1
articles.summary: The Trojans weren't the only dominant Big Ten team in Week 1, but Michigan's offense is a mess and other teams struggled as well
articles.body:
Big Ten football came back this past week. There were almost two big upsets the Big Ten was on the wrong side of; the best teams in the conference mostly looked the part as title contenders. USC , after another great win, could be ready to join that conversation.

Here is what we learned following Week 1 in the Big Ten:

Michigan will fall short of expectations this season

Michigan was seconds away from getting handed one of the biggest upsets in quite some time. Bryce Underwood was great on the last drive, but he still left a lot to be desired in this performance. This was not a convincing win for the Wolverines , and if anything, they should not be looked at in the same way they were prior to the game. This team will not be the contender they were expected to be.

Julian Sayin-Jeremiah Smith connection will be unstoppable this year

As expected, the Ohio State Buckeyes offense looked great in game 1. Julian Sayin was amazing last season in his first season as a starter. His connection with Jeremiah Smith, however, looks automatic. Jeremiah Smith had 8 catches for 156 yards and 2 touchdowns, all in the first half. While Julian Sayin was 21-for-25 for 320 yards and had 3 touchdowns on the day. The Sayin-to-Jeremiah Smith connection will be a big problem for every team they face this season. For USC to knock off the Buckeyes, they will just have to match that production on offense.

Indiana will be just fine at quarterback this year

The Hoosiers lost Heisman winner and #1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza this offseason. It would have been safe to assume that quarterback would be a position that regressed this season. Josh Hoover helped lessen the doubt by delivering a great season-debut performance. Hoover showcased toughness, and he delivered strikes all game long. Hoover had 4 touchdowns and 231 yards on the day. He won over this team and gave the reassurance that the Hoosiers will still be a force this year.

Oregon came into Week 1 as the title favorite, and they got punched in the mouth early by Boise State. They went down 17-7 to start the game against the Broncos. Thankfully for the Ducks , this team found its rhythm, and Dante Moore was special in the second half. Oregon was good enough in the end to come out victorious. However, the slow and sluggish start still paints the picture that Oregon is not the dominant force many thought they were.

Rutgers will be the worst team in the country this season

In Game 1 of the season, Rutgers suffered one of the worst Power 5 losses in quite some time. UMASS dominated Rutgers in this game. It was 24-7 at halftime. UMASS got the biggest win in its program against Rutgers. UMASS looked like the better team, and that does not bode well for Rutgers hopes of being competitive in the Big Ten this season. KJ Duff looked like an NFL receiver, but he can only do so much. Duff was the lone bright spot for the Scarlet Knights. Rutgers made UMASS's season, while their season looks over just as soon as it started.

articles.title: Paul Ince explains what “very, very good” Man United star must add to his game
articles.summary: 2Former Manchester United midfielder Paul Ince has urged Kobbie Mainoo to step up this season. The Red Devils invested heavily in the midfield this summer, s...
articles.body:
Former Manchester United midfielder Paul Ince has urged Kobbie Mainoo to step up this season. The Red Devils invested heavily in the midfield this summer, signing Andrey Santos, Youri Tielemans, and Carlos Baleba.

However, Mainoo remains a vital cog in Michael Carrick's system, especially following his rise under the English manager in the second half of last season. The 21 year old played a crucial role in United's third-placed finish in the Premier League, starting all 16 games he was available for since Carrick's arrival in January.

Mainoo was initially linked with an exit from Old Trafford at the beginning of the year, but signed a new deal this summer. The highly-rated academy graduate's intelligence, calmness, and abilities on the ball have made him indispensable for the Red Devils of late.

The English midfielder has also added a layer of steel to his game after rubbing shoulders with Casemiro . However, Ince believes there are still a few areas where the youngster can improve.

Speaking to the Mirror , Ince urged Mainoo to take control, drive forward, and add a goalscoring threat to his game. He said: "With the greatest respect to Ipswich, if they are going to come to United and play open football, I could still do a job against them. It goes without saying that Kobbie has to do that week in, week out."

"And I want to see someone who takes control of the game. I don't want to see someone who just gets the ball and passes it square. Or moves it on to Bruno Fernandes. I want to see someone who drives forward, who plays one-twos."

"How many shots does he have in game? When I played I used to make sure I had at least three or four shots in a game. And, essentially, he is playing exactly the same role as I did. There is more to his game than just passing it and letting the likes of Bruno and [Matheus] Cunha do their stuff."

"He can add a lot more to come. He can get more shots off. He can drive with the ball. He's got good feet, he's got lovely feet. All the attributes he has got, he needs to start showing them more."

"You've got to believe in how good you can be and not play the safety first football. Potentially, he is a very, very good player."

Ince also argued that United should have signed a new left-back or a striker instead of investing around £130 million in Santos and Baleba . He continued: "I don't understand why United would buy Santos for £50m and Baleba for £70m when they already have Mainoo."

"I felt there might be other areas where the money could have been spent. Perhaps in the full-back area or a striker to help them push for the top two or three."

United were linked with several left-backs this summer, including Newcastle United's Lewis Hall, but could not strengthen the position. Meanwhile, a new striker was reportedly on INEOS' agenda as well, with Freiburg's Igor Matanovic named among the shortlisted candidates.

However, the Red Devils ended the transfer window without signing a new striker as well, while Joshua Zirkzee, who was heavily linked with an exit, also ended up staying.

Mainoo was among the better players on the pitch for United in the disappointing 2-2 draw against Everton at the Hill Dickinson Stadium on Sunday, 6 September. The Englishman is yet to reach his peak and has the potential to become a game changer for the Red Devils.

articles.title: Garrett Cleavinger is still a great pitcher
articles.summary: I’m sure you are rolling your eyes at this headline, but please, hear me out!
articles.body:
Garrett Cleavinger had a 3.31 ERA and 3.40 FIP through July. Since the beginning of August, however, the results haven't been there, with a 10.38 ERA and 6.79 FIP. He has even improved his first pitch strike rate from the high 50s to the low 70s between both samples, so it's not like his command has completely disappeared. We'll look at his key performance indicators to see what's going wrong:

Cleavinger is really not doing anything fundamentally different compared to what he was doing most of the year before August. His underlying data is still solid and suggests the pitcher the Rays trusted earlier this season is still there. A .385 BABIP has played a major role in his recent rut while a subtle shift in his fastball location has made his stuff a little less deceptive. That BABIP is roughly 100 points higher than his .283 career mark. Some of that is almost certainly variance, but his recent fastball location issues may be contributing at the margins.

Cleavinger has allowed a .390 wOBA for his career on fastballs located on the arm-side third of the zone compared to a .212 wOBA on fastballs located on the glove-side third. He primarily throws both of his fastballs across the zone glove-side and down to that optimal spot as evident in his heat map from March through July:

But lately he's been missing more to the arm-side as we can see in his August through September heat map:

The fastball still plays there to some extent, but more importantly it loses some of the cross-fire deception and awkward angle Cleavinger creates when spotting it glove-side. He throws his breaking ball to a similar spot across the zone, so landing the fastball there helps the two pitches play off each other. Failing to consistently hit his fastball locations diminishes the effectiveness of his arsenal. He loses some of the deception and tunneling that makes his entire pitch mix difficult to attack.

Because Cleavinger's delivery doesn't appear meaningfully different, I wonder if the problem could be addressed through his visual cue rather than a mechanical adjustment.

When Cleavinger throws his fastball, his catcher initially sets up high and near the middle of the zone before sliding toward the glove-side target. Here's the setup, which is typically more in on lefties:

A similar cue is used against righties, although it's typically closer to the middle of the zone:

Because Cleavinger still looks like himself mechanically, a potential solution to getting his fastball glove-side and down again could be to shift the catcher set-up. He's missing arm-side with a high and middle cue, so shifting the cue to high and more glove-side could help him in regaining feel for locating his fastball. This wouldn't necessarily need to be a permanent change. Cleavinger has a long track record of spotting his fastball at its intended location. The idea isn't to change his target, but to change the visual cue he uses to find it.

With Cleavinger already on the IL, the timing could actually work in his favor. The break gives him an opportunity to work through the adjustment without having to solve it in a game, but there is some risk in making an adjustment this late in the season. Relievers live on routine, and changing a visual cue in September could create more uncertainty if it doesn't immediately improve his command. With the postseason approaching, there's little margin for experimentation.

Cleavinger doesn't need to reinvent himself. His underlying performance suggests the pitcher the Rays trusted earlier this season is still there. He needs the BABIP pendulum to swing back toward him and, more importantly, needs to regain the fastball location that makes his unusual delivery and arsenal so difficult to hit. If he can consistently get back to glove-side and down, the rest of his arsenal should follow.

articles.title: Longhorns backup QB KJ Lacey flashes potential in win over Texas State
articles.summary: In the Longhorns season opener, KJ Lacey gave a preview of what the future holds. The backup QB played well in relief of Arch Manning.
articles.body:
On Saturday afternoon, Longhorns fans got a preview of the future as Texas rolled to a 59-7 win over Texas State . With the Longhorns comfortably ahead, quarterback Arch Manning was replaced after throwing for over 300 yards and four touchdowns for KJ Lacey. The talented freshman only played a few series, but he made the most of his snaps.

In relief of Manning, Lacey completed six of his seven passes for 55 yards. While he was unable to find the end zone, the former top recruit showed great decision-making and averaged seven yards per pass. He also got some action in the running game with three yards on two carries.

While Lacey's playing time was limited, his success came as no surprise. He was ranked as the 19th-best quarterback in his class by 247Sports . They also ranked the Saraland High product as the 15th best player from Alabama. Due to his stellar play in high school, Lacey was named Alabama's "Mr. Football" as a senior, which made him a popular name for teams in need of a QB and a big pickup for Texas.

As Lacey frustrated the Texas State defense, he also received praise from the Longhorns coaching staff, including head coach Steve Sarkisian. When asked about Lacey's play in the second half, Sarkisian said, " I just think there's a level of consistency and comfort in the system. He definitely has playmaking ability."

Although his opportunities will be limited, Lacey has shown that he can step in when needed. Through his first two years as a Longhorn, Lacey has completed seven of his eight passes for 62 yards. Those numbers should continue to improve as long as the Longhorns offense meets expectations.

Regardless of how often Lacey gets on the field this year, he will be an exciting player to watch with plenty to prove on a team with national title hopes.

articles.title: Top performances from Oregon Ducks transfers in Week 1
articles.summary: Oregon Ducks transfers are all around the nation in college football. Which former Ducks had the best performances in Week 1 of the 2026 season?
articles.body:
Following — and in some cases, prior to — the Oregon Ducks ' College Football Playoff Semifinal loss to the Indiana Hoosiers in January, 31 players entered the transfer portal, looking for more play time elsewhere. For an Oregon roster that routinely fields 20-30 blue-chippers each recruiting class and can only start a finite number of players, it's the cost of doing business in this day and age of college football.

That was the case for the Ducks this offseason, especially after the announcement that as many as seven likely 2026 NFL draftees made the decision to return, retaining their spot as starters. That led to an influx of transfers, especially along the defensive line.

With Week 1 of the 2026 college football season nearing a close, it's time to check on those former Ducks. With the level of talent that's departed the program in recent years, there's bound to be strong performances by former Oregon players each week, and we're here to highlight that.

Here are the best performances by former Oregon Ducks in Week 1, beginning with a running back who saw little time in 2025 in Eugene as a highly-coveted incoming transfer but is back to dominating on the field.

Analysis: All of last season at Oregon, which ended up being four games due to redshirting, Makhi Hughes carried the ball 17 times for 70 yards. In his first game with the Houston Cougars, he carried the ball 17 times for 98 yards and a touchdown while catching two passes, helping propel the Cougars take down the Oregon State Beavers , 33-20.

S Kingston Lopa — California Golden Bears

Analysis: Considered to be one of the top transfer safeties, Kingston Lopa followed former Oregon defensive coordinator Tosh Lupoi to the California Golden Bears. In their opener against the UCLA Bruins , Lopa showed exactly why he was so coveted in intercepting a pass and registering a team-high six tackles. However, the Golden Bears defense couldn't corral the Bruins' offense, as they allowed 45 points in the defeat.

Analysis: The star of Oregon's spring game in 2025, Luke Moga was slated to be among the backups for starter Jack Layne with the New Mexico Lobos — but plans quickly changed when Layne had shoulder surgery just weeks ago, ending his season. While Moga didn't start, he was the better of the two Lobos quarterbacks as he completed 13-of-17 passes for 116 yards and a touchdown, leading New Mexico to a 38-7 win over Central Michigan.

Analysis: Moving close to home for his final two seasons of eligibility, Jayden Limar was the lead back for the Washington Huskies in their 24-10 victory over the Washington State Cougars in the Apple Cup on Sunday. While the Washington offensive line had trouble providing much movement, Limar still totaled 47 yards and a game-clinching touchdown on 12 carries.

Analysis: The lone running back available for the Ducks alongside Dierre Hill Jr. in the CFP Semifinal, Jay Harris set a career-high with six carries for 53 yards and a touchdown for the Kansas State Wildcats in their 71-3 win over Nicholls State. Harris' touchdown came late in the third quarter of the blowout, and he was outpaced in carries by two other backs. It's likely that he's serving as a reserve for the Wildcats this season.

Analysis: Having redshirted at Oregon in 2023 before a season with the Georgia Bulldogs, Collin Gill has become a star for the Charlotte 49ers over the past two seasons. He had 35 tackles a season ago, and totaled 11 tackles in the first game for the 49ers, a heart-breaking 43-41 loss to The Citadel in triple overtime.

WR Justius Lowe — San Diego State Aztecs

Analysis: Serving as a solid depth receiver in 2024, Justius Lowe's role diminished in 2025, as he went from 21 catches to just six. He then transferred to San Diego State and led the team in receiving yards in the opener against Portland State, finishing with 56 yards on two catches including a 40-yard touchdown grab.

Analysis: One of seven players along the defensive line to depart from Oregon, Ashton Porter joined Hughes at Houston. In his debut against Oregon State, Porter notched three tackles and a sack after totaling 1.5 sacks in three seasons with the Ducks.

Analysis: After having 32 tackles and two sacks last season, Blake Purchase was one of the main players blocked from a starting job at Oregon when the defensive line returned. He showed out in his Ole Miss Rebels debut on Sunday in front of the nation, finishing with five tackles, half a sack and 1.5 tackles for loss. The Rebels took down the Louisville Cardinals in a thriller, 41-38.

articles.title: What is the Detroit Lions’ ceiling for the 2026 season?
articles.summary: Is a Super Bowl on the table for the Detroit Lions’ 2026 season? We discuss the absolute ceiling for the team.
articles.body:
It's become the battle cry of Detroit Lions fans annually after the previous season has come to its disappointing conclusion.

There haven't been many more recent seasons more disappointing for Lions fans than the 2025 campaign. For the prior four seasons, it had been all about growth. 2022 ended with Detroit's thrilling Week 18 win to kick the Packers out of the playoffs and make a statement that the Lions are coming. 2023 was the closest this team has ever come to making a Super Bowl, with an unbelievably run deep into the playoffs. In 2024, Detroit posted a franchise high in regular season wins (15), only to see it come crashing down with a second-round exit in the playoffs.

After each of those seasons, it felt like it was inevitable Detroit would eventually break free of the postseason torment and finally reach the elusive Super Bowl. We said, "Next year is our year" with actual confidence, not an ironic twinge.

Then 2025 happened. Detroit took their first clear step back as a franchise under coach Dan Campbell, and it certainly has some wondering if the Lions can right the ship and get back to championship contention. So today's Question of the Day is:

What is the Detroit Lions' ceiling for the 2026 season?

My answer: Well, if you believe ESPN's prediction model and their full 2026 NFL season preview , Detroit's ceiling for wins is a 13-4 record, and they've got a 71.4 percent chance of making the playoffs. So, certainly, making the playoffs should be considered the expectation, not the ceiling.

But how far can this team make it? Can they really orchestrate a Super Bowl run? Does their roster compete with the consensus contenders like the Los Angeles Rams, Buffalo Bills, and Seattle Seahawks—the three teams with the best Super Bowl odds?

I would contend that they do. Their offense is filled with superstardom, from Jared Goff to Jahmyr Gibbs to Amon-Ra St. Brown and Penei Sewell. And as I pointed out last week, the team's depth on the offensive and defensive lines are deeper than they've been in quite some time .

Sure, there are questions about how quickly the newly formed offensive line can gel together. And there is certainly warranted concern about both the starting-level talent and depth at cornerback. Every team has questions, and every roster has some talent gaps. We here in Detroit tend to obsess over those things, as they are typically the things that sink this franchise.

And they could very well again this year. But at the same time, the Lions' schedule looks easier to start the season, which should give the offensive line some grace to continue to build chemistry. And while the cornerback room certainly looks like the team's biggest weakness, Detroit's investment in pass rush and assignment-sound safeties could be enough to mask that weakness as much as possible.

So do I think the Super Bowl is on the table for the Lions this year? Absolutely. Will it require several things to go Detroit's way in 2026? Yes, and that is the case with every single Super Bowl winner in NFL history. So pour a little Kool-Aid in your coffee this morning.

articles.title: Gabriel Agbonlahor wowed by “disgusting” Liverpool man he slammed last year
articles.summary: Gabriel Agbonlahor was full of praise for Alexander Isak following his goalscoring display against Ipswich last Friday.Liverpool secured their first three po...
articles.body:
Gabriel Agbonlahor was full of praise for Alexander Isak following his goalscoring display against Ipswich last Friday.

Liverpool secured their first three points of the Premier League season under new boss Andoni Iraola, with the Swede registering a quickfire double in the first half of their clash at Portman Road .

The efforts take the former Newcastle star's tally to three goals, on par with Erling Haaland and Bruno Fernandes in the top-flight scoring charts.

A confidence-boosting display for Alexander Isak

There were, perhaps, questions to be asked of Liverpool's opposition regarding the quality of defending in the opening 10 minutes of action.

However, the quality of the combination between Cody Gakpo and Isak (not to mention the Sweden international's finish) likewise deserves equal emphasis.

"He looked very sharp. Maybe we can get a centre-half on to discuss Greaves' defending – shambolic at the back," Agbonlahor spoke on TalkSPORT.

"But the way he took that first one, Jeff – people will say goalkeeper should save it – but the way he striked it [with] so much power, great first touch. The second one, that's what we used to see from Isak at Newcastle; twisting and turning and getting the finish off.

"He just looked a lot more sharp, making a lot of runs in behind. Gakpo's balls were fantastic. When you give him the service, he will score goals. He just needed a bit of time to bed in."

Quite a far cry, we have to say, from the pundit's explosive comments following on from Isak's switch from St James' Park to Anfield the summer before last.

"Who do you think you are, mate? Who do you think you are?" Gabriel Agbonlahor spoke on TalkSPORT back in 2025. "It's disgusting. What that club's done for you."

After a tumultuous 2025/26 campaign played against the backdrop of the 26-year-old's controversial transfer and fitness issues stemming from the lack of a proper pre-season, the tide seems to be turning.

Analysing Alexander Isak's potential turnaround at Liverpool

(Photo by Justin Setterfield/Getty Images)

You have to say that Liverpool's opener against Ipswich felt like a very "Liverpool goal". A turnover forced by Milos Kerkez's aggressive pressing inside our own half before the ball was moved vertically at pace, with Isak positioned neatly between centre-back and left-back. Eight seconds from the turnover and Liverpool found their opening goal.

To refer back to Gabriel Agbonlahor's prior analysis, it's worth pointing out that our record-breaking striker signing has hardly just discovered how to get himself into shooting positions.

The problem was that Liverpool lacked the appropriate pace on the flanks and the creativity down the middle, not to mention the setup from the head coach to platform the central striker.

Look, Liverpool aren't signing a centre forward for £125m if the plan is to stick with what the status quo was under Jurgen Klopp and, then, briefly, Arne Slot for a single season.

And with the right winger market ultimately letting us down this summer, with top target Yan Diomande initially appearing to decide for PSG before later having his head turned by Real Madrid, we have to double down on the concept of platforming the striker.

With rapid wide options like Victor Munoz, Rio Ngumoha and Bradley Barcola available, that should help provide Alexander Isak with the space he needs to flourish. And it certainly helps when options like Cody Gakpo can use their evidently notable creative prowess to take full advantage of our main man's clever runs into space.

This could be a great season for Alexander Isak.

New York Giants general manager Joe Schoen promised last week that the Giants were not done adding to their defensive line, saying they would "probably" add a veteran player to that group this week.

Well, per ESPN's Jeremy Fowler , the Giants have done just that. The Giants are adding Dean Lowry, entering his 10th NFL season, to their practice squad.

Lowry, 32, is a 6-foot-6, 296-pound defensive end who was a fourth-round pick by the Green Bay Packers in 2016. Lowry spent seven years with the Packers, one with the Minnesota Vikings, and the last two with the Pittsburgh Steelers.

Lowry has played in 132 regular-season games with 85 starts. Statistically, he has 16.5 career sacks and 271 tackles.

Lowry spent last season on injured reserve due to a torn ACL. He was released by the Steelers in the cutdown from 90 to 53 players.

articles.title: Team USA survives incredible flop attempt by Italian player at FIBA Women’s World Cup
articles.summary: Team USA hung on for a three-point win as Cecilia Zandalasini's attempt to sell a call failed.
articles.body:
Team USA survived a scare and walked away with a 55-52 victory against Italy at the FIBA Women's World Cup on Sunday night to stay atop Group D. The Americans were able to prevail despite Caitlin Clark scoring one point and going 16-for-56 from the floor as a group. It was certainly not a convincing performance but a win is a win and the U.S.'s stifling defense played a huge part down the stretch.

Italy had a chance to tie things up and force overtime on the game's final possession but Cecilia Zandalasini's three-point attempt missed well wide. The brick came after one of the most egregious attempts to draw a foul call from the officials you will ever see. One that, if it worked, would have been an all-time bad call.

Zandalasini whipped her head back and to the left as Jackie Young closed in hard to provide pressure, reacting as though she had been poked in the eye. Check out the replay and see if you think there's any chance any contact was made.

Zandalasini was irate after not being rewarded for the theatrics and confronted an official about the decision. Eventually Italy's coach, Andrea Capobianco, was able to calm her down.

After the contest, Zandalasini struck a different tone while apologizing for her actions in the final seconds and after the buzzer.

"I'd like to apologize for how I reacted in the end to the opposing team," she said during her team's press conference. "There were a lot of emotions today, but I should have kept them inside a little better. I want to apologize to the referees. It is just that when I wear this jersey, it is a different beast. And now I feel embarrassed for how I reacted."

Now, a lot of people will be worked up about this and take little pause before calling it a brutally unconvincing flop. But one shouldn't hate the player, they should hate the game. Given the moment, it was actually smart strategy to try to get to the line as the possession appeared dead in the water and officials feel great pressure in crunch time as well. If there wasn't a reward structure in place for selling calls, hoopers wouldn't do it on both ends of the court all game long.

articles.title: Super League Frantic Friday: Wigan Warriors and Leeds Rhinos go for League Leaders' Shield, Wakefield Trinity and Warrington Wolves battle for third
articles.summary: Wigan Warriors need to win in Round 27 to clinch the League Leaders' Shield; Warrington Wolves and Wakefield Trinity are still in contention for third; the regular Super League season concludes with Round 27 from Thursday September 10 live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
There is a trophy up for grabs, positions to be decided and teams vying for a home play-off spot.

With that in mind, there are outcomes galore and a 'Frantic Friday' of action not to be missed.

Five games, all kicking off at the same time, that will decide the outcome of the regular season and how the play-offs will shape up.

So what exactly is at stake? Let's take a look...

The battle for the League Leaders' Shield will go down to the wire and be decided in the final round of Super League action.

Wigan Warriors' emphatic 40-8 win at Leeds Rhinos in their top-of-the-table clash has left Matt Peet's side in pole position for the honour.

Indeed, Oli Partington believes they have "one hand" on the trophy that would secure them a domestic double.

However, they need one more win to wrap that up when they take on Catalans Dragons on Friday.

They win that match and the Shield is theirs.

However, if they lose, Leeds Rhinos can take the League Leaders' Shield, for the first time since 2015, with a win over Hull FC.

If both teams win or if both teams lose, then it is Wigan's.

The trophy will be presented on Friday evening whichever way it goes.

Play-off positions: Battling for a home play-off spot

The teams that finish in third and fourth after the regular season will guarantee themselves a home play-off spot.

Third will then play sixth, with fourth taking on fifth for a spot in the semi-finals.

Warrington, who sit in third, host in-form Toulouse Olympique who are desperate for a win that could see them finish higher than their French rivals Catalans in eighth position.

A win for Warrington over Sylvian Houles' team and third place in the table is secured.

However, fourth-placed Wakefield Trinity could still usurp the Wolves as they aim for their best finish in the Super League era.

To do that they would need to win the mouth-watering game at Leigh Leopards, who sit just two points behind them in fifth, and see Warrington lose.

If Leigh win by a healthy margin, they could move into fourth and drop Wakefield to fifth.

If Leigh lose and sixth-placed Hull KR beat St Helens, then the defending champions could jump up from sixth to fifth.
